title: pthread library perhaps should be linked to libdronelink.a
body:
Hi Julian, as we see that DroneLink is built as a [static library](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L52); why so ? Is it not meant to be used by multiple applications ?

And, `libdronelink.a` itself [uses threads](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/core/udp_connection.h#L7); but it is not linked to pthread lib. The [example takeoff_and_land](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/example/takeoff_and_land.cpp#L8) itself is using threads so linking thread make sense.
But if an application doesn't intend to use threads don't link it as part of their build; then app build would fail again for the same reason! 

Ideally, `libdronelink.a ` should be linked to pthread library. And, I think its not possible if its static library.
Please share your thoughts about this and correct me if I am wrong.

Thanks.
Shakthi

At the moment we have one [example](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/tree/master/example) in the example folder. We're going to have more in future, so propose a dir structure like
**/example/takeoff_and_land/** or **/examples/takeoff_and_land/**

title: Guide/example for creating plugins
body:
Dronecore is the officially supported layer for providing access to PX4, via MAVLink (of course there are other integration points, like the RTSP bridge). We're expecting others to extend the API via plugins, for example, to add support for peripherals that interact with the system via custom MAVLink messages.

We need a simple but realistic example of a plugin and an associated guide that shows how it works/what you need to do to write one.

title: A picture is captured always during a mission execution though its not requested by application

title: We should be able to track connection status of Device objects other than by callback
body: The suggestion is that it should be possible to detect whether Device is connected from the object itself. This would allow a client to iterate the vector of devices and only handle those that are connected - without having to separately manage tracking connection/and disconnection.

title: DroneCore::ConnectionResult enum inconsistent name
body:
The rest of the classes all just use "Result" for the enum name. I think we should be consistent.

This would also allow us to consistently name the method for getting the human readable string (e.g. `result_str`

It MAY also be worth deciding on a more descriptive name than just "Result". E.g. CommandResult, MessageResult, SendResult, APIResult etc.

title: add_XXX_connection() could be better named
body: Using connection here means that any description of the API is riddled with the word connection - since we also have to connect to the device. It is probably worth using something like  `add_XXX_port()` to make it clear that this is just part of the whole "connect to devices" process.

title: Only report change information in appropriate callbacks
body: For arming, landing, flight mode etc it is likely that you will only want to get callbacks notified when the values change. The suggestion is to allow clients of the API to specify whether notification should happen on every message, or just when the value changes.

title: Plugins should not try resending on disconnected devices
body:
For example, if you disconnect the device but then try landing, the plugin will still try to send the message, and to resend it. 
```A
Altitude: 2.679 m
Disconnected device with UUID: 4294967298
Landing...
sending again, retries to do: 3  (21).
sending again, retries to do: 2  (21).
sending again, retries to do: 1  (21).
Retrying failed (21)
Land failed:Timeout
```
I am not sure what the correct behaviour should be, but certainly it is not a resend. Ideally the user should be notified of this when they try to make the method call - typically there is a device disconnected "Results".

title: Example showing best-practise for handling device disconnection and reconnection
body:
We need to show how a user might best handle disconnecting from the vehicle and reconnecting, both when managing 1 vehicle and when managing multiple vehicles. I'd expect a client app to:
- be able to detect and report disconnection/connection
- stop the device from attempting to send messages
- reset to a sensible state based on what the vehicle is actually doing when you connect - e.g. if already flying, not attempt to send commands to arm etc (unless the vehicle ignores those).

title: Add support for NED missions
body:
Generally when writing "reusable" drone applications and examples it is much better to be able to specify positions in NED co-ordinates rather than absolute positioning - because then you can specify a pattern of movement and re-use it as needed.

NED missions are supported by MAVLink, but not PX4. The proposal is to add a sensible API in DroneCore with a backend that can be replaced by PX4 support when that comes available.

title: Add frame conversion distance libraries

- Get the GPS coordinate for a particular body-frame.

This could provide the backend for https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/100 , and additionally make it easier for users to implement their own movement based calculations.

title: Dynamic plug-in infrastructure
body:
DroneCore has its functionality built with compile-time plug-ins such as `Action`, `Mission`, `Telemetry`, etc. When DroneCore is built, we can choose which plug-ins we're interested in. Build chooses plug-ins in `plugins` directory and generates `DevicePluginContainer` class and methods to access to the "choosen" plug-in objects. It is necessary to build DroneCore if we wanted to add a new plug-in to it.

We're interested to add new plug-ins which DroneCore will pick it up run-time. Theoretical approach for this is [here](https://px4.slack.com/archives/C68J8H32A/p1506435370000733).

However, as we're interested to developing language bindings using gRPC; gRPC requires `.proto` files for each of the plug-in to be known at compile-time.
We're yet to investigate the feasibility of both (gRPC & dynamic plug-in). 

Updates on this activity will posted here.

title: Exposing Flight mode APIs in core/device_impl.h
body:
We have [methods](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/core/device_impl.h#L86-L89) in `DeviceImpl` for PX4 param get/set; but we don't have methods to know/change flight mode in `DeviceImpl`. These methods are useful for plugins. 

Below are the plugins each of which maps to a **PX4 flight mode**:
- [Offboard plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/offboard/offboard_impl.cpp#L48)
- [FollowMe plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/core/device_impl.h#L86-L89)
- [Mission plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L682)

As of now (in above plugins), we're doing the hard way by using  `MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE`. I think it makes sense to expose a method for the same as part of `DeviceImpl` interface. 

At present we've a [public API to get flight mode](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/telemetry/telemetry.h#L392) is part of `Telemetry `plugin. If other plugins want to know flight mode, they can't call `Telemetry` plugin API (which creates plugin dependency). So it is suitable and intuitive to move some of the useful flight mode APIs from `Telemetry` plugin to `Device` as well.

title: Name change proposal for "Device" class to "Drone" or "Vehicle"
body:
This is regarding name change proposal of the class `Device`, `DeviceImpl`, etc.
We've named the library & API after **drone**, as in **DroneCore**, it makes sense to name its core service class to be `class Drone`, or at least `class Vehicle` (in QGroundControl) rather than `class Device`.

Cons of having `Device` name is that it is likely to be used for Ground Control Station, Mobile device also.
In other words, GCS is a device as well;
When we say `Vehicle`, there is no room of confusion whether it is Drone or Ground Control Station.

If DroneCore is also intended for general Robotics application, then probably `Device` might sound good.
Kindly share your thoughts, opinions.

Thanks.

title: TCP connection drop causes high CPU usage
body:
I connected DroneCore to a TCP server using `add_tcp_connection()`. If the added TCP connection drops, DroneCore will just spin in `receive()` of `TcpConnection`, because `recv()` returns immediately with 0. This causes 100% CPU load and shouldn't be desired behavior when the socket is disconnected.

I've fixed the issue by just setting `_should_exit` flag when `recv()` returns with 0 in receive thread. Certainly not the best solution but does the job for me. The dead connection still stays in DroneCore's connection list, so it would be nice if it could either be reopened manually through API or DroneCore tries to keep up connections itself.

title: Device never gets connected again after heartbeat timed out
body:
When heartbeats time out of a connected `Device`, the `Device` gets disconnected and never connected again. So both `is_connected()` (with only one device) and `is_connected(uuid)` (with uuid of previously connected device) never return true again. This also affects at least the `Device` thread update rate (100ms instead of 10ms).

Looking at the `device_impl` code, ` set_disconnected()` resets `_target_uuid_initialized`, but not `_target_uuid`. Now autopilot version is not requested again in `process_heartbeat()`, because `_target_uuid` was previously set to a nonzero value. Target uuid is never initialized and `Device` never gets connected again.

Fixes I tried, both work for me:

- `set_disconnected()` resets `_target_uuid_initialized`, `_target_uuid` and `_target_uuid_retries`.

-  `set_disconnected()` just doesn't reset  `_target_uuid_initialized`, keep the uuid of the prevously connected device (an obtained uuid never changes in my application, this might not work for others).

title: Support MissionItems for LAND, TAKEOFF
body:
We need [MissionItem](https://docs.dronecore.io/v/develop/en/api_reference/classdronecore_1_1_mission_item.html) functionality for takeoff and landing. These items should attempt to properly support common options for MC, Plane and VTOL (where they differ). Specifically I would hope that we could have a single land and single takeoff item to support all of these:
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_LAND
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_LAND_LOCAL
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF_LOCAL
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_VTOL_LAND
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF

Once these exist they also need to be supported in the mission import and download from vehicle and added to tests.

There was some discussion originally that these are not needed because 
* MC automatically takes off if no takeoff is present
* Action API supports these functions.

They are needed because:
* MC automatic takeoff does not allow you to specify any takeoff behaviour
* Plane and VTOL do not automatically takeoff if no takeoff item is present
* QC plan import and download from vehicle can end up being different in round trip.

To me this just makes sense.

title: DroneCore handles only one component
Autoupilot type used for GCS is wrong
body:
[Currently](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/f308f020205c08d930e1acaa849b332e365d4965/core/device.cpp#L289) GCS type (in Heartbeat) is [MAV_AUTOPILOT_GENERIC](http://mavlink.org/messages/common/#MAV_AUTOPILOT_GENERIC) (its a type for autopilot! not for GCS).
However, MAVLink documentation recommends to use [MAV_AUTOPILOT_INVALID](http://mavlink.org/messages/common/#MAV_AUTOPILOT_INVALID) for GCS.

I know that we documented right way of using it; however the example shouldn't mislead new users.

title: Choosing reference over pointer
body:
It is recommended to use references when we can, and pointers when we have to.
(Reference: https://isocpp.org/wiki/faq/references#refs-vs-ptrs)

We can replace `Device *_parent` to `Device & _parent` as I see that, its possible. We initialize while activating plugin and never modify it. Also, we have a method (below) that actually gives, **a reference to a device**, not pointer. 
```cpp
Device &device(uint64_t uuid);
```

Consider, below piece of application code:
```cpp
Device &device = dc.device(); // we get reference to device
auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(&device); // why pass its address ?

// Why not pass it as-is?
auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(device);
```
I just noticed this.
@julianoes, was it done intentionally for some vital reason? If not, then we can find similar usages and replace them properly.

title: Return vectors by value in C++11
body:
In below piece of code:
https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/a2b9db92f83e53bcce75c611f6e9b473f4341562/core/dronecore_impl.cpp#L210-L211
although we clear vector in every invocation, we made it as `static`; this is because we want to return a reference to it:
https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/a2b9db92f83e53bcce75c611f6e9b473f4341562/core/dronecore_impl.cpp#L207


_We can return a vector **by value** in C++11, because it has move semantics, which will simply move local vector into callers' vector (hence no copying). Thus we gain advantage of time complexity._


**References:**
- http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector/operator%3D
- See Bjarne Stroustrup's answer in https://isocpp.org/blog/2013/01/quick-q-is-it-still-bad-practice-to-return-a-vector-from-a-function

title: Rendering of reference and pointer parameters in markdown script
body:
Currently a parameter with a ref or pointer renders with a space after the ref like this: `Device & somedevice` or `Device * somedevice` (rendering is fine value parameters).

The question is, should this render as `Device& somedevice` or `Device &somedevice`

(as an aside, the second format is slightly harder, because for pointers, care needs to be taken to make sure the * is not interpreted as "make text italic".

This originates here: https://github.com/dronecore/docs/pull/107#discussion_r174682278

title: Rename "Mavlink" stuffs to that of "MAVLink"
Maintain a connection instance per component in case of UDP
body:
Right now we've maintain one connection per System (one or more components).
This creates problem if there are more than one component in a system.

Consider below scenario:

- After we receive heartbeat from a component A of a system on udp port (say, 14540), we fill source ip/port details as part of connection instance. When we receive heartbeat from another component B of the same system, **_Core assumes System IP may be changed due to Wifi disconnection._**
- While we're sending commands/messages, we need to make sure we send to IP/Port of the corresponding component whom it is meant to be.

I think, to support multi-component in core, we shall have one connection per component. We should map each component with its connection to make this happen.

Please provide better suggestions, if any.
It is linked to #304 . And hopefully the fix should be part of #310 .

title: Improving logging
body:
Right now, we're logging DroneCore logs on console. Generally its a practice to dump all the debug logs to a file. We could save them onto say, `build/default/logs/dronecore.log`.

Then, a user may simply run on a terminal:
```tail -f build/default/logs/dronecore.log```

So, we can add **more debug/info logs** in the code (as it won't collide with application console logs) which are really helpful to analyze issues. For ex: say, arming/takeoff fails. We can easy look into logs to see whether **all the necessary things went well** or not.

PS: _As discussed in Slack, we're planning to add this in future (not right now)._

title: Its time to switch Coding style to Clang format
body:
Clang format is most popular C++ coding style: http://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormat.html
Benefits:
- We can also integrate this in git using [git-clang-format](https://github.com/llvm-mirror/clang/blob/master/tools/clang-format/git-clang-format) or add git pre commit hook.
- Clang has a [static analyzer](https://clang-analyzer.llvm.org/).
- It will rearrange header file inclusion order alphabetically (@JonasVautherin was this earlier).
- Supports various styles.
  - LLVM A style complying with the LLVM coding standards
  - Google A style complying with Google’s C++ style guide
  - Chromium A style complying with Chromium’s style guide
  - Mozilla A style complying with Mozilla’s style guide
  - WebKit A style complying with WebKit’s style guide

Reference:
http://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormat.html
http://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormatStyleOptions.html
https://clang-analyzer.llvm.org/
https://clangformat.com/ - Interactive guide and builder.

@julianoes @JonasVautherin @hamishwillee .

title: Implement thread pooling for user callbacks
body:
In order to prevent user callbacks from blocking the receive thread like it happened in #373, we need to make sure not to call user callbacks in the receive thread.

This was fixed in #387 but the change introduces a memory leak and potentially a lot of overhead by using `std::async` and spawning a thread everytime (depending on the compiler).

FYI: @shakthi-prashanth-m @anitha-suresh 

https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/d0c47bb3c749738feb9d04db807e9fba93c7688e/core/mavlink_system.cpp#L878-L889

We should decide if that is something to implement ourselves or use a library/dependency.

## [v0.4.0](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/tree/v0.4.0) (2018-04-26)

[Full Changelog](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0)

**Implemented enhancements:**

- Rename "Mavlink" stuffs to that of "MAVLink" [\#329](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/329)
- Support for `COMMAND\_INT` [\#326](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/326)
- Return vectors by value in C++11 [\#319](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/319)
- Class name change: Device to System [\#318](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/318)
- Choosing reference over pointer [\#314](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/314)
- Add support to include Doxygen tags \code and \endcode [\#259](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/259)
- Rename `camera\_action\_delay\_s` to `loiter\_time\_s` in MissionItem class [\#249](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/249)
- Connection URL for DroneCore applications [\#244](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/244)
- FollowMeImpl::set\_config\(\) returns immediately though Device didn't confirm [\#221](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/221)
- Cross-compile the backend for iOS [\#213](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/213)
- Cross-compile the backend for Android [\#212](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/212)
- Have one gRPC server library for each plugin [\#211](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/211)
- Dynamically load plugins in dronecore\_server [\#210](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/210)
- device.h should become a library [\#209](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/209)
- Build core as a library [\#208](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/208)
- Build each plugin in its own library [\#207](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/207)
- Clarify FollowMe::Config::min\_height\_m and follow\_dist\_m  [\#204](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/204)
- Exposing Flight mode APIs in core/device\_impl.h [\#193](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/193)
- FollowMe API feels inconsistent [\#191](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/191)
- Follow Me has no example [\#189](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/189)

- Add Follow me example [\#217](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/pull/217) ([shakthi-prashanth-m](https://github.com/shakthi-prashanth-m))

**Fixed bugs:**

- Mission items are not cleared before building them up [\#348](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/348)
- DroneCore application \(GCS\) should NOT mix up with System/Device [\#317](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/317)
- Takeoff example exits before vehicle is ready [\#307](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/307)
- Autoupilot type used for GCS is wrong [\#305](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/305)

- TCP connection drop causes high CPU usage [\#201](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/201)

title: Decide how to pass callbacks to API
body:
I see that we have inconsistency in the way callbacks are passed into the C++ API.

Some of the APIs use pass-by-value:
```
void subscribe_plugin_something(const subscribe_plugin_something_callback_t callback);
```

Others use pass-by-reference:
```
void subscribe_plugin_something(const subscribe_plugin_something_callback_t &callback);
```

From my understanding, pass-by-value leads to a copy (shallow or deep?) of the function object and therefore adds overhead, however, it prevents the case where the passed callback goes out of scope which can lead to a segfault.

@shakthi-prashanth-m @JonasVautherin opinions?

title: attitude_euler_angle() returns "NaN" for Pixhawk 2.1 Cube
body:
### Using Raspberry Pi 3 B+

- If running with the Pixhawk 2.1 cube (with motors, gps, lidar, flow, etc powered) , attitude_euler_angle().yaw_deg returns "NaN". (Also returns "NaN" for roll, pitch, and quaternion values)
- If running the sitl simulation, attitude_euler_angle().yaw_deg returns the correct attitude

### Using Linux Ubuntu 16.04.3
- If running with the Pixhawk 2.1 cube (Just connected straight to the Cube, no peripherals are powered), attitude_euler_angle() also returns the correct attitude.
- If running the simulation, attitude_euler_angle() returns the correct attitude.

### Possible Leads
1. I have a video of receiving the correct attitude from mid-May. The major difference there is the v1.8.0 Firmware update released June 19th. At the time of the video, it was (most likely) running v1.7.3 released Jan. 6th. I was having trouble reverting back to that firmware to check, so I haven't tested that yet.
2. Telemetry().longitude/latitude/velocity also are null on the Pixhawk 2.1 cube if the gps isn't locked (flashing green). This makes sense, so there might be a different hardware component that affects attitude like the gps affects the above values.

calibration without STATUSTEXT commands
body:
While building my own flight stack I have hit an issue with calibration.

```C
void calibration_callback(const Calibration::Result result, const Calibration::ProgressData progress)
{
cout << "progress " << progress.progress << " result " << (int)result << endl;
}

...

auto calibration = make_shared<Calibration>(system);
calibration->calibrate_accelerometer_async(calibration_callback);
```

The situation is:

1. my quad receives [COMMAND_LONG](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#COMMAND_LONG) with [MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION) id
1. it starts sending [COMMAND_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#COMMAND_ACK) with MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS as result
1. In the end it sends one [COMMAND_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#COMMAND_ACK) with MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED

I am not sending [STATUSTEXT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#STATUSTEXT) commands

The issues are:

1. The callback is never called. I think that it is related to
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L180-L198
Commands with MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS result do not get propagated - that it known issue. The problem is that `calibration_callback` is not called even when the last command with MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED is received. That can be fixed by inserting something like
`call_user_callback(_calibration_callback, Calibration::Result ::SUCCESS, Calibration::ProgressData(false, NAN, false, ""));` here:
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/plugins/calibration/calibration_impl.cpp#L203-L205
1. It is not possible to run the calibration for the second time simply because `_state` is still set to `State::ACCELEROMETER_CALIBRATION`. It should be cleared `_state = State::NONE;` here:
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/plugins/calibration/calibration_impl.cpp#L203-L205

If the current implementation is working for you then it is probably because the flight stack also sends [STATUSTEXT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#STATUSTEXT) commands.
https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/e5d4e0e8510cd02bfbfe5d629e1a2e4ff49549c9/plugins/calibration/calibration_impl.cpp#L261-L338

title: Mission progress won't send event until aircraft reaches the following waypoint
body:
This happens for mission items with loiterTimeS = .nan, cameraAction = stopPhotoInterval/no action. We do not get mission progress event until aircraft reaches the following waypoint.

We get a mission progress event every time the drone reaches a waypoint.
The issue seen is, if you have a waypoint mission (for example 10 waypoints), where 5th waypoint has 'loiterTimeS = .nan' & 'cameraAction = .none' and the 6th waypoint has 'loiterTimeS = 1' & 'cameraAction = .takePhoto', then when the vehicle reaches 5th waypoint, we do not receive mission progress event and when the vehicle reaches 6th waypoint, we receive the mission progress event twice.
This happens for mission items with loiterTimeS = .nan, cameraAction = stopPhotoInterval/no action.

title: Add offboard plugin to backend and language wrappers
body: It would be nice to add support for offboard to the language bindings.

title: Automate dependencies for Linux and Windows
body:
When building the MAVLink test suite setup fails on Windows and Linux because there are missing dependencies. As discussed  [here](https://github.com/Auterion/mavlink-testing-suite/issues/13#issuecomment-470413491) it would be better if the SDK is able to install its own dependencies.

@julianoes Just a reminder :-)

title: Adding support for ArduPilot
body:
## Context

A while ago, @peterbarker worked on adding support for APM in the SDK ([here](https://github.com/peterbarker/DroneCore/tree/ardupilot)). More recently, @jinchengde (and others) started looking into that, again. The goal of this issue is to discuss the high-level requirements and architecture.

## Benefits for APM

The project is architectured in such a way that everything relies on a C++ MAVLink implementation. Making this implementation compatible with APM means that APM will also get the language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java) and future ones like [Javascript](https://github.com/mrpollo/DronecodeSDK-JavaScript)).

The interface common to all our bindings is defined [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) and is used to auto-generate language-specific APIs (e.g. using RxSwift in Swift, RxJava in Java, and asyncio in Python).

## SDK architecture (overview)

The SDK can been seen as composed from 4 parts:

1. The [interface definition](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) (protobuf files), common to all the languages (C++, Swift, Java, Python). Each proto file is considered a "plugin", which is a group of (MAVLink) features.
2. The C++ [MAVLink implementation](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK), which actually maintains a connection to the drone and does the MAVLink logic.
3. The [backend](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/tree/develop/backend), which exposes the C++ implementation of (2) as a messaging server through the interface of (1).
4. The language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java)), which implement (1) to communicate with the backend (3).

At the lowest level, each plugin (defined by one proto file) is a C++ library. The backend uses those libraries, as can been seen [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/backend/src/CMakeLists.txt#L38-L46).

title: Rename to MAVLink SDK
body:
There are some concerns with the "Dronecode" branding of the project, such as:

* Confusion between the Dronecode Foundation and the SDK
* Confusion on slack (#sdk vs #dronecode)
* Makes it sound like it is limited to PX4 and may be offensive to other communities (even though there is some work regarding adding support for APM in #728)

The proposition here is to rename it to "MAVLink SDK", as it is a MAVLink implementation and a high-level API in different languages. As a consequence, the project would move to the MAVLink organization.

And RFC has been open on the [MAVLink repo](https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/pull/15) to see if that would be acceptable from the MAVLink side.

Please feel free to share your opinion and discuss it here :blush:!

title: Migration to MAVLink organisation
body:
Copying @hamishwillee's message on the PX4 Slack, to keep a record of the discussion.

The MAVLink dev team accepted the "MAVLink RFC Proposal" so we'll be taking the Dronecode SDK into the MAVLink organisation and renaming it to the "MAVSDK": https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/blob/master/text/0011-mavlink-sdk.md

### Code


* [x] Agree on new names for SDK repos
 => Will be `MAVSDK`, `MAVSDK-Proto`, `MAVSDK-Swift`, `MAVSDK-Python`, etc.
* [x] Move all SDK repos into github mavlink org
* [x] Agree new names for namespaces and other code items
 => The documentation and official name is `MAVSDK`, but the code doesn't have to follow that. We will generally prefer lowercase (i.e. namespace: `mavsdk::`), and we may capitalize if necessary (e.g. `class MavSdk`).
* [x] Update code in line with new names
* [ ] Update READMEs with appropriate new links to repos and docs
* [x] Make an official first release. Would this be 1.0?
 => The release will not be 1.0, but just the continuation of current releases, each repo going at its own speed. The Python SDK will be released as `0.1.0` on pip ASAP.
* [x] Make sure all old repositories redirect correctly

### Docs


* [x] Design of new logo & tagline
 => Taken care of in #750.
* [x] Confirm name of docs repo in mavlink org [I think `sdk_docs` to `mavsdk_docs`]
* [x] Move docs repo into mavlink org
* [x] Update head revision docs API reference
* [x] Update docs guide materials
* [ ] Review/update docs on marketing/positioning. Ie where it is hosted and the goals.
* [x] Decide what to do about previous releases/docs. These all will refer to the Dronecode SDK.
* [x] Propose that we delete all the old ones and start from scratch with a master release and initial release
* [x] Re-sync via gitbook
* [x] Get new domain/URL. 
 Current: `https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/`. Proposed: `https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/en/`. This is probably easier than try to do `mavlink.io/mavlink`, `mavlink.io/mavsdk` etc.
* [x] Themes updates
 The theme for the SDK becomes more like the mavlink.io one: https://mavlink.io/en/
* [x] Other dronecode sites will need to have theme updated to point to SDK and any notes about SDK updated too.
* [x] Make sure all old docs links redirect correctly

### Dronecode Website


* [ ] Update top bar
 This is likely to be SLOW process.
* [x] Update SDK page and other mentions.

### Channels


* [x] Discussion board category rename
  * [x] Docs updated (develop, master, 0.16)
  * [x] Update category post link to URL when SDK URL moves: https://discuss.px4.io/t/about-the-mavsdk-category/4234
* [x] Slack channel rename to `#mavsdk`
  * [x] Docs updated (develop, master, 0.16)

title: Move protoc generation out of cmake and version generated files
body:
@julianoes, @thomasetter: I'd like to have your opinion on that :blush:.

We use protobuf + gRPC in `mavsdk_server`, and therefore generate code with the proto compiler (`protoc`), at build time. I believe this should change, mainly for the following reasons:

* We will soon want to autogenerate more code, using our own protoc plugin. It will make the autogeneration a bit more complex (will require to build a python module, etc), and therefore I don't feel like keeping that in our CMakeLists. We already have separate scripts for that [in Swift](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Swift/blob/master/tools/generate_from_protos.bash) and [in Python](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/blob/master/other/tools/run_protoc.sh).
* We will autogenerate the C++ header files, and it would make sense to version them, so that we can link to the github files in discussions. We already do that [in Swift](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Swift/tree/master/Sources/MAVSDK-Swift/Generated) and [in Python](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/tree/master/mavsdk/generated).
* When cross-compiling, we currently need to build for the host first, so that we get `protoc`, and then we can cross-compile. It takes time (e.g. on the CI), and sometimes it doesn't work. For instance when using dockcross on my machine, my host-built `protoc` relies on a version of glibc that is not available in the dockcross container, and therefore `protoc` doesn't run there.

For those reasons, I believe it makes sense to generate the files separately, and version them.

The new workflow would look a bit like this:

1. If you don't need to generate the files (typically when cross-compiling), you just run `cmake` (configure) and  `cmake --build` (build), and rely on the versioned generated files.
2. If you need to generate the files, you:

    a. run `cmake` (configure) so that you get `protoc`
    b. run `generate_protos.sh`
    c. run `cmake --build` (build)

@thomas.etter: Note that this would break the changes you did for automatically re-generating when the proto files change.

title: Yaw/heading not accessible in MissionItem class
body:
It seems that `MissionItems` don't include a vehicle heading, which would be really helpful. This could be accomplished by adding the following methods to the `MissionItem` class:

- `yaw_to()` (double degrees from N): Rotate the vehicle to the specified angle after reaching position set by `set_position()`.
- `yaw_for()` (double seconds): Rotate the vehicle for the specified time after reaching position set by `set_position()` at rate specified by `set_yaw_rate()`.
- `set_yaw_rate()` (double rotation speed in deg/s): Set the target rotation rate for vehicle yawing. 
- `set_yaw_departure_ned` (double degrees from N): Set the heading for after mission item (transition to next mission item)

I am not sure the last method would be needed if the heading specified by `yaw_to()` could be maintainted between waypoints. If it could, the last item would be redundant. If multiple headings are desired at a given position, they could simply be stacked as a series of mission items with the same position, but differing values set by `yaw_to()`. 

I have a project wherein we need to be able to specify the vehicle heading because we have a directional antenna attached. I'd like to transition to Mavsdk, but need this heading control capacity.

title: MAVSDK - setup_udp_remote - no MAVLink being received using Passthrough
body:
**Description:**

I have tried to connect to QGC to send/receive MAVLink messages using _MAVSDK 0.21.3_ setup_udp_remote, utilizing MavlinkPassthrough plugin. It seems like connection created this way is not able to receive MAVLink messages.

I've prepared a demonstration application to show just that:

**Demonstration:**

1. Clone https://github.com/VarkAven/mavsdk_udp_issue 
2. Build it using standard cmake build (make build directory, source CMakeLists.txt etc...) (Make sure you have _MAVSDK 0.21.3_ installed on your system)
3 Launch QGC (3.5.5), _set it up to receive UDP connections_ (QGC -> General -> check UDP field in "AutoConnect to the following devices")
4. Launch the demo application, **no arguments required**.
5. Observe that **"Received PING response!"** **does not appear.** Neither **"Received MAVLink message. It's msgid:"** despite being subscribed and having a callback to receive every MAVLink message.

**Some more information:**

Connecting to QGC via bare Linux API UDP socket and sending MAVLink Ping request yields QGC responding with Ping response MAVLink message. So QGC has Ping micro service implemented.

A telemetry subclass ie `telemetry.raw()` that gathers sensor information and current readings available through mavlink. Also, IMO the sensor reading timestamp "time_boot_ms" (ex: https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#DISTANCE_SENSOR) is especially useful from my perspective for sensor fusion and filtering to approximate vehicle state.

title: Add Avoidance Plugin to MAVSDK
body:
These are my first thoughts regarding adding an avoidance plugin to MAVSDK.

Requirements: In my mind, as per the rest of MAVSDK, this plugin should be self-contained and therefore not depend on any other frameworks such as ROS. In fact, I don't think that the core Avoidance plugin should even implement any actual avoidance logic; it should just expose a high level API to the [MAVLink Path Planning (Trajectory) protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/trajectory.html). This will allow for a flexible way to implement Mission mode obstacle avoidance - see [PX4 Obstacle Avoidance](https://docs.px4.io/v1.9.0/en/computer_vision/obstacle_avoidance.html) for more details. If any avoidance logic for i.e. point cloud via LiDAR is implemented, it should be kept separate.

The two main architectures that come to mind for me are:

1. A "polling" approach - the user calls avoidance.receive_trajectory() which returns a list of waypoints. These waypoints are then altered as needed to "avoid obstacles". Finally, avoidance.upload_trajectory() is called on the new waypoints. This procedure is repeated in a loop at 5Hz.
2. A "subscribing" approach - the avoidance API allows you to subscribe a function as a callback. The existing trajectory is passed into the callback, processed, then outputted in the function return. In this approach, MAVSDK handles registering and triggering the callback, and the user only implements the callback.

Off the bat, the subscribing approach seems cleaner to me. However, there are a few considerations to make before deciding on and implementing an approach:
- Although I'm not sure if it will be performant enough, I would like to leave room for writing gRPC bindings for other languages.
- If considering other languages bindings, callbacks might be implemented differently, so this will have to be figured out.
- Callbacks require the avoidance logic function to be somewhat contained, and if other variables/code are required, it might be hard to reference other code. I'm not sure to what extent this is a problem, as I haven't done much async/callbacks in C++ before.

I'd love to hear people's thoughts to decide on an architecture, so I can start developing it!

title: Organize & Cleanup Receiver System & Component ID Handling
body:
Hello, I was looking into the source code and I found quite a few FIXME's in `mavsdk_impl.cpp` regarding how different system and component IDs are handled. I created this issue so we can try to fix these issues, and to offer my thoughts on how they should be implemented as well as hear other people's ideas.

1. [L256](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L256): Agreed, there are a couple things wrong here. First of all, we should not be setting the SID to a known CID, that's bad usage of the definitions. However, I don't think we should simply hard code in another value. See point 3 for my thoughts on a better approach.
2. [L258](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L258): Again, this time at least we are setting the CID to a value designated for a Component ID (but incrementing it by 1? :thinking: ). This is still a fairly arbitrary value, and furthermore is hardcoded.
3. Personally, I think the `Configuration` structure is rather limiting. It forces the user to use a specific SID and CID (which is automatically decided for them) which further has the implication of only being able to successfully run 1 instance of MAVSDK at a time (well, maybe 1 per `Configuration` but you get the idea). Furthermore, the hardcoded values are set to some weird values! :thinking: 

My suggestion is: as far as API goes, start with a `void set_mavlink_id(uint8_t sid, uint8_t cid)` or similar which allows for manual user setting of the SID and CID. The current `Configuration` idea can still remain as a feature but should be refactored to something like `set_auto_mavlink_id(MavType type)` which makes more sense to me - it allows the user to have MAVSDK automatically choose an *appropriate* SID and CID based on the type of system the user is implementing with the SDK. Also, I personally feel that setting either the SID and CID or the `MavType` should be mandatory at the constructor level, but I'm not sure how others feel about this?

Now for what those auto values should be:
* For `MavType GCS`: Quoted from MAVSDK source: "Usually QGC identifies itself with sysid 255" - we should just pick a standard ID that we want to be the default MAVSDK SID, and stick to it. According to the MAVLink documentation, it is good practice to count GCS SIDs down from 255. So I'm throwing the value `245` out there, as its reasonably close to the top but leaves some room for multiple QGC/other GCS instances to be run. In reality any SID would work, and we should probably do at least some basic searching before deciding on one, to minimize conflicts (at least with existing open source GCS). The CID should be set to `MAV_COMP_ID_MISSIONPLANNER` as this is most likely what the user needs (stated in docs as "Component that can generate/supply a mission flight plan (e.g. GCS or developer API).", which is most likely the usage of MAVSDK in the context of a GCS.)
* For `MavType CompanionComputer`: This is a bit more difficult, As the FIXME says it should be autodetected. The best way to do this would probably be to read incoming `MAV_HEARTBEAT` messages until one with the CID `MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT1` is discovered, and set our SID to the source SID of that message. As for CID, `MAV_COMP_ID_PATHPLANNER` would probably be the most idiomatic, considering the companion computer is usually involved in path planning, obstacle avoidance, etc.
* For `MavType Autopilot`: As far as default values go, the existing is fine - 1 as SID and and `MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT` as CID.

4. [L263](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L263): See point 3.
5. [L78](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/master/src/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L78): This is a tough one. Could someone explain to me why we are blanket ignoring all QGC messages? Is this a QGC specific thing, or do we just not want to handle messages from other GCS? If that's the case, we should again use heartbeat to get a list of GCS based on `MAV_COMP_ID_MISSIONPLANNER` or similar, and ignore anything in that list. This seems restrictive, however, as you can't communicate with other GCS... i.e if 2 MAVSDK instances were communicating with each other. Either way, checking a specific SID is a bad idea - I for one run multiple QGC instances with different SIDs, so this wouldn't work off the bat. Would something bad happen if we didn't ignore GCS messages? Instead of "blacklisting", maybe we could "whitelist" by deciding on a per-message basis if we are capable of handling it?

These are just my thoughts - please feel free to comment and share ideas. Once we have a good idea of what we want to do, I can open a PR and implement the changes!

title: Generalizing MAVSDK for non-autopilot control
body:
Traditionally, MAVSDK has been used to connect solely to a drone in order to control it; connecting to other peripherals has been more of an addon than a main feature. While this is definitely the main use case of MAVSDK, I think it would be nice to be able to use MAVSDK as a more generic high level platform for any MAVLink communication. This would increase the number of use cases and platforms MAVSDK can be deployed to, and also allow some very interesting new possibilities. Below are some comments on what the current state of affairs is and what can be done to improve this without sacrificing ease-of-use.

The base `Mavsdk` class define the source system and component, which defines the local side of the communication. With the recent addition of the `Configuration` class, this is fine - the system and component ID can be changed without restrictions, and there are sane defaults. From here on, though, things get a bit more complicated.

The `System` class, although designed to connect to any MAVLink compatible system, is in reality only tailored to connect to a single autopilot. This causes problems, obviously, when connecting to anything *other* than the autopilot. Peripherals such as gimbals and cameras are supported; however, they are all connected to the parent `System` rather than a parent `Mavsdk`, which makes more sense to me. As a result, you need to connect to an autopilot before getting access to any peripherals. Additionally, although MAVSDK can be used to control an autopilot from a companion computer, how MAVSDK handles connecting to a different component on the same system is uncertain and definitely undocumented.

To be completely honest, from looking into the core source code, I feel the code to handle system and component ids is very messy; a good portion of it is probably very old code, but I think we can do better. For example, there is a lot of hard-coding "let's throw away messages from these ids", "lets assume this component ID means this", etc. This leaves very little room for anything that deviates from the standard "I have a ground station which connects to my drone, both with standard IDs." I'd like to be able to use MAVSDK for more complex things including intra-system (inter-component) communication. I'm happy to take charge of cleaning some of it up + documenting it, if we can agree on what to do! For starters, I think we should all read https://mavlink.io/en/guide/routing.html :smile: 

I'm not sure the best way to do this, since I don't want to break the current API (create a System from a Mavsdk, create plugins from the System). One idea I had was to create a `Component` or similar, which is a more high level representation of a target that MAVSDK can connect to. The `Mavsdk` class can then search for and connect to multiple `Components`, and the existing `System` would be a type of `Component` (not sure if System is even the right word for it, in that sense, but I'm hesitant to break the current API). Or we could rename `System` to `Component`, and enable different plugins based on the type of `Component`, such as Autopilot, Companion Computer, Gimbal Device, Camera, custom component, etc.

Anyway, let me know what you guys think! Again, I'm happy to implement the changes!

title: Timesync adjusting outgoing message timestamps
body:
The usual method for timesync with mavlink is that outgoing messages are sent with the sender's clock source, and the receiver should translate it into their own time frame. However, we've seen now with MAVSDK that after an initial timesync exchange it adjusts the clock source for _outgoing_ messages. This causes massive confusion on the flight controller side, since it was trying to adjust timestamps on incoming messages to what the clock source on MAVSDK was _before_ it did the timesync. This might be the root cause of #960 ? It can also cause instability in both timesync algorithms since they try to estimate each other when the offset is constantly changing, instead of estimating a single offset which should be mostly constant.

To fix this, outgoing messages should be timestamped with a consistent clock source (preferably CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, ie something that isn't affected by time jumps or temporary clock slewing on the host system), and only incoming messages should be adjusted via the timesync message.

FYI @irsdkv , @JonasVautherin suggested I tag you since you contributed this. Do you see any problems here? Would you have time to fix this?

Thanks @DanielePettenuzzo for the investigation.

title: Is tune example working?
body: We are testing tune example, but it does not work at the moment.

title: LibreSSL download is broken?
body:
The error appears when trying to build mavsdk_server with the following command:
`cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_BACKEND=ON -Bbuild/default -H`
It looks like either the download server is down

labels.name: beginner
labels.description: A good issue for someone that only gets started

body:
We should add support for multipart statustext messages as specified in https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink/pull/1295.

Here https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/138ee4acebfbfa5875425048423014cb454ebee4/src/core/system_impl.cpp#L216-L258

title: Segmentation fault when request Euler angle
body:
You have a segmentation fault when you request information about attitude like `set_rate_attitude_async`. Issue comes from the atan2f not know.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/67862f45ea86a33a1392183f94e9be423746b3ba/src/plugins/telemetry/math_conversions.cpp#L13

labels.description: A good issue for someone that only gets started

body: Back when MAVSDK was named differently we also called the instance of `Mavsdk` different. Leftovers are still sprinkled all over the integration tests and examples. It would be nice to get them cleaned up.

title: MAVLink v2 signing example?
body:
Hi,
As far as I know, mavlink v2 signing function is not implemented on QGC, so does MAVSDK.
Is there any plan to implement mavlink v2 signing in MAVSDK with example?

title: Error compiling takeoff_and_land example on Docker.
body:
Hello,

I'm having an issue while running the takeoff_and_land example on a docker machine.

title: Mission generation should use NAV_DELAY instead of sending two waypoints on the same location
body:
From @julianoes:
> The reason MAVSDK sends the same lat/lon twice in a row is because it adds a LOITER_TIME right after a NAV_WAYPOINT. The right approach would be to use NAV_DELAY [...].

Which is implemented in PX4 for quite some time (I verified). The reason PX4 rejects now waypoints that are on top of each other is because the path between those waypoints is not defined (zero distance). Often we however need to know where the vehicle is coming from geometrically and allowing N waypoints on the same location would force us to traverse the mission multiple times and quite a bit forward and backward, increasing the complexity of the autopilot in terms of memory, execution time and also in terms of our ability to QA and certify the code.

So in short: This is undesirable in principle and navigation commands should not exist in the same physical location one after the other.

title: Who should initiate TIMESYNC?
body:
This is related to #1169. Looking at MAVSDK's timesync implementation, it seems like we send TIMESYNC messages in two situations:

1. In `process_timesync`, where we receive a TIMESYNC message and answer to it
2. In `do_work`, where we actually initiate the TIMESYNC exchange

Is it meant to be like this, or do different components have different needs? E.g. the "master" (I would guess the autopilot) could be the one initiating the sync, and he other components may or may not answer depending on their needs, right?

@irsdkv: your insights would be appreciated :slightly_smiling_face:!

title: Camera triggering in QGC survey missions not supported.
body:
Currently there is no support for the `MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST` mission item, which is the standard way of triggering in a survey mission. Currently a survey mission imported with` import_qgroundcontrol_mission` will be executed but without the camera doing anything.

There is a test case for `MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST` in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/plugins/mission/mission_import_qgc_test.cpp  but no implementation yet.

title: Offboard doesnt want to enable after a is_active() check.
body:
MavSDK version v0.35.1

I am having an issue where the offboard does not want to enable. It seems like a few things...a race condition with a bad check (mavsdk side) and a bad way of checking the state of offboard (my side).

I was checking if the _offboard->is_active() but that was always true (because _mode != Mode::NotActive - it was PositionNed) before calling _offboard->start()...this was not a good way of doing it because even when the is_active switched to false so I could start the offboard (which happened periodically randomly) it would respond back with a failure because 
```
        if (_mode == Mode::NotActive) {
            return Offboard::Result::NoSetpointSet;
```
(offboard_impl.cpp)^^


How I fixed it: 

In process_heartbeat() i changed `_mode != Mode::NotActive` to `_mode == Mode::NotActive` . This caused the race condition of the NotActive being set too quickly to not happen anymore...

AND 

I, instead of checking is_active(), I check that `_flightMode != Telemetry::FlightMode::Offboard` and this allowed it to go into the offboard mode and respect my movement commands. 

My code is [here.](https://github.com/mcelhennyi/NXP-HoverGames-2/blob/ebc11e9577710f4cf036a230838d943761f902f8/code/src/system/agent/Agent.cpp#L305) 

I am not sure if the changes I made are proper and dont want to PR them without a discussion about this issue first. 

I also have been conversing with @JonasVautherin [here](https://px4.slack.com/archives/C68J8H32A/p1612241663087100) about this issue if you would like some more context.

title: Support multiple batteries
body: As discussed [in this thread](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Swift/issues/189#issuecomment-802221631), I think that `telemetry.battery()` should expose a list of batteries (instead of only one). title: Structure Cmake for Cpp package managers
body:
It would be useful to be able to use MAVSDK with cpp package managers (Hunter, Conan etc) for automatic dependency resolution. Instead of depending on a `SUPERBUILD` or local dependencies.

I've been implementing this library with [hunter](https://github.com/cpp-pm/hunter) and have found success by doing the following:

0. `SUPERBUILD=OFF`
1. Remove git commands from Cmakelists.txt, such as getting version from git tags
2. Don't use git submodules 
3. Remove Find modules provided by https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/cmake/Modules/
4. Use common lib names when linking: 
`JsonCpp::jsoncpp` -> `jsoncpp_lib`
`tinyxml2::tinyxml2` -> `tinyxml2`


This won't work for `mavsdk_server` but it is a start. There is likely to be more changes to this to get it to work (for Hunter I have included Hunter_gate but obviously this differs for each manager :) )

title: Feature req: pkgconfig for building
body:
The "standard" way of including libraries in linux is pkgconfig mechanism. This tells what headers and libraries must be included in the compilation process. Almost any library in linux distros ship with pkgconfig metadata file. Pkgconfig can be used from any build system including cmake and qmake.

Mavsdk currently does not ship with pkgconfig and it's not obvious how to build correctly when using other than CMake as build system.

title: MAVSDK timeout tuning
Provide Autopilot/Server functionality for MAVLink services
body:
It would be exceptionally useful to have MAVSDK provide server functionality for MAVLink microservices. 

There is currently a gap missing in MAVLink, the raw data types are provided by the MAVLink headers but the implementation of the microservices (Command, Mission, Heartbeat, Parameters etc) is still up to the user to implement. This can easily lead to fragmentation of the standard with the services. It also makes MAVLink integration into existing systems difficult.

MAVSDK does a good job of tackling this from a GCS/Companion side, but API is not currently suitable for the autopilot side as it was built on the assumption we're communicating with a MAVLink autopilot that implements the services we require. MAVSDK connects as a client.

There is a real case for server implementation in MAVSDK along these lines and MAVSDK could be used as a basis for a MAVLink autopilot. While obviously not for embedded platforms, there are certainly use-cases for this on non-PX4/Ardupilot autopilot systems but also in testing frameworks. In addition MAVSDK could bridge existing autopilot systems with MAVLink.

I propose MAVSDK implement the following plugins:

- Mission server (`MISSION_REQUEST_INT` workflow from autopilot side)
- Command server (subscribe to commands, ack, etc)
- Parameter server
- Message server (`MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE`? `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` support?)

I've recently documented what MAVLink messages + parameters MAVSDK requires in order to function, I can list these as it would probably be a useful starting point for these services.

title: Mavsdk instances should not share mavlink_status_t
body:
It turns out that `Mavsdk` instances will share `mavlink_status_t` if they are in the same compilation unit. This happens for instance when two `Mavsdk` instances are created in an integration test to talk to each other. In this case, they will access the same `mavlink_status_t` which is allocated `static`, so they will share the `seq` field.

The `static` status comes from here:
https://github.com/mavlink/c_library_v2/blob/636fae5ca34eff6007344718755d78fcdf94238e/mavlink_helpers.h#L29

The solutions I see are:
1. Use `_pack_chan()` everywhere, instead of `_pack()`. This would require all plugin code to be changed and also would require the Mavsdk instance to detect other Mavsdk instances using some sort of global data structure. Both things I would like to avoid.
2. Try to allocate the status in `Mavsdk` and use the `MAVLINK_EXTERNAL_RX_STATUS` define: https://github.com/mavlink/c_library_v2/blob/636fae5ca34eff6007344718755d78fcdf94238e/mavlink_helpers.h#L25 I'm not entirely sure how the mapping would work though.
3. Check the MAVLink C++ library to see if it handles it differently.

This can be observed in the Ftp integration test, e.g.

```
cmake --build build/default -j8 && MAVSDK_MESSAGE_DEBUGGING=1 build/default/src/integration_tests/integration_tests_runner --gtest_filter="FtpTest.TestServer"

body:
This is used as a tracking issue for ArduPilot incompatibilities.

Some, but not all MAVSDK plugins have ArduPilot support. This ticket will list **known** compatibilities and incompatibilities. If not listed, the state is unknown - It may work, it may not.

Please comment if you have tested functions and can confirm/deny working.

If you would like an ArduPilot feature included in MAVSDK, please contribute.

### Known API **functional** with ArduPilot :

- Telemetry
  - `set_rate_position_async`
  - `set_rate_gps_info_async`
  - `health_all_ok`
  - `subscribe_position`
  - `subscribe_heading`
  - `subscribe_raw_gps`
  - `armed`
- Mission Raw
  - **NOTE:** First mission item must be home position for ArduPilot
  - `upload_mission_async`
  - `subscribe_mission_progress`
  - `clear_mission_async`
  - `start_mission_async`
- Action
  - `arm`
- MAVLink Passthrough
  - `subscribe_message_async`
  - `send_command_int`
- Param
  - `set_param_float`

### Known **Broken** API

- Mission
  - Needs to account for first mission item being home in Ardupilot
- Probably much more :)

title: Can the gRPC server be started before mavsdk-server discovers/connects to a system?
body:
In some cases, applications using mavsdk may start before the UAV system starts and is discovered by the mavsdk-server. In this case, clients intending to connect to the mavsdk-server will effectively have to block because the gRPC port will not be available.

Alternatively, if the gRPC server is up and the port is available, the clients won't have to block and the channels that are running in the background will automatically start receiving data once the UAV system is discovered.

The earlier versions of the mavsdk-server used to behave in the same manner which made client-side implementation quite easy.

title: Support multiple callback-subscribers
body:
MAVSDK allows to subscribe to new information with callbacks, like for example updates to the Position telemetry:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7244ace0d7b223e8e7618d8736769f4f2a2ef1f3/src/plugins/telemetry/include/plugins/telemetry/telemetry.h#L990-L993

In the implementation only one callback function is registered, and subscribing a second time would simply remove the previous subscription silently:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7244ace0d7b223e8e7618d8736769f4f2a2ef1f3/src/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L2075-L2079

I would love to have the possibility to add multiple callbacks / subscribers. This would also lower the chances, that I ruin someone else's subscriber in a collaborative code base by overwriting that person's callback function.

title: server plugins should not be limited to a single system
body:
As I have been working on the camera server plugin, I've noticed a problem with the way the current plugin architecture creates a plugin instance per system (i.e. `CameraServerImpl::CameraServerImpl(System& system) : PluginImplBase(system)`). The problem is that the plugin state is per system when really it needs to be global. This means that consumers of MAVSDK have to do lots of extra work to ensure that each plugin instance for a single camera remains in a consistent state with the others. Example: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1699/commits/1528f0cf05fcae55be6941694f7d935d0fa378b0.

I suppose other server plugins haven't noticed this problem before since they probably only communicate with one system. However, cameras need to communicate with both an autopilot and a ground station at the same time.

I think a solution to this would be to create a new "server" plugin type that is initialized with `CameraServerImpl::CameraServerImpl(Mavsdk& mavsdk) : ServerPluginImplBase(mavsdk)` instead. Then a single plugin instance could receive and send messages to any number of systems. (And broadcast to multiple systems as required by [CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED).)

Otherwise, we should reconsider https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/274#issuecomment-1039591231, particularly the `Set*` methods. Basically, the camera server plugin should have no state and everything is handled by callbacks to user code. I'm not sure this is really possible though since the callbacks themselves are considered part of the state.

title: Camera::set_setting_async send request only to the first camera
body:
Working with a system with two cameras (#1705) i noticed that the camera settings requests using (`Camera::set_setting_async`) are  always sent to the first camera, regardless the real camera target.

The problem resides in the  `MAVLinkParameters` class that in the` MAVLinkParameters::do_work` function use predefined constants depending on the `work->defined` value has target components.

I want to try to add a more generic way to set the component target in  the MAVLinkParameters class.  

My question is: It's better to (1) add a component id argument (with a default value) to already existent functions like `SystemImpl::set_param_async`, or is better to (2) add a new whole set of functions that will accept also a component id?

title: std::optional for CommandLong always returns true. Causes fault on Ardupilot
body:
[Line 429](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.cpp#L440) of mavlink_commands.cpp,  is a check to see if particular parameter on the command long has been set using the contextural conversion of std::optional. If it has not been set, the the value is initialised to certain values depending on whether the auto pilot is ardupilot or not. 

It does appear that this check always returns true, regardless if the param has been set. This maybe due to the initialisation of the values in CommandLong to NAN. This will result in ardupilot autopilots throwing a SIGFPE and closing the connection. This may be the cause of some of the problems in #728 and elsewhere particularly when SITL is used. 

I'm not sure of the correct solution but perhaps not initialising those parameters is probably an option?

title: Cannot use QGroundControl simultaneously with an active mavsdk script in hardware testing
body:
In hardware testing, QGroundControl accesses the serial port of my telemetry radio. This does not allow me to launch a MAVSDK script. My current modus operandi is to run the script without QGC but that is no longer viable. I have tried enabling port forwarding on QGC and changing the ```add_any_connection("serial:///``` to  ```add_udp_connection```.
This does result in the MAVSDK script connecting to the drone while QGC is open. But during mission upload, it fails as the ``` while (telemetry.health_all_ok()``` does not return true and the mission upload fails.
The output from the MAVSDK script is that it discovers many systems and components.
Is there any way to find out the correct system/component ID of the flight firmware?
Are there any alternative ways of enabling port forwarding/ keeping QGC open while being able to run a MAVSK script?
It happens smoothly in SITL where the MAVSDK script connects to the local PX4 flight firmware being launched on my system while QGC remains connected to it.

I can right-click on SITL, import that file to ardupilot and I can make this flight in AUTO mode. 

I am trying to instead of uploading the mission through SITL to upload it from a custom android app. I have tried to implement this with Mission Plugin. As I have understood this is not working for ardupilot. 
I can see that @bazfp has already made this work with plugin MissionRaw. I have seen here [https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1568](url) that "First mission item must be home position for ArduPilot". I cannot understand if this has to be a MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT instruction and then I have to add the MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF command?

If anyone has made this work, since there is no example in MAVSDK-Java nor MAVSDK-Python about mission_raw plugin, could you please provide me with the shortest possible example(seq 0, 1 and 2) in any language(C++, Java, Python) so that I can understand the process of deploying such commands?

title: Question: How can I get the value of channel 10 (1100 / 1900) ?
Mission download corrupt with low timeout
body:
If I set the timeout low (e.g. 0.2s) and try to upload and download a mission over and SiK radio, the mission can suddenly be shorter.
While it is expected that we might hit timeouts trying with such a low retransmission timeout, it's not expected that the mission transfer is supposedly ok but then not corrupt.

title: Battery telemetry raw current values
body:
Hi,

In the current version 1.3.1 [battery telemetry](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/66b7b2e4736c884f3c530ec42376b10c80de857d/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L1151) only contains battery id, voltage and remaining capacity percentage.

Is there a way to get the raw current readings, too, as the MAVLINK battery message does contain it, and if not can it be included in later versions of MAVSDK?

Thanks in advance.

title: Get current speed of the drone and Change heading when drone in hold mode
body:
Hi,

I would like to get the current speed of the drone as telemetry when it is doing a mission. Could not find it in telemetry API. Is the ground velocity the current speed of the drone?
And I would also like to change the current heading of the drone when it is in HOLD mode.  Is there anyway to do it ?

Thanks in advance.

title: Follow Me messages getting sent in burst form (2 at once)
body:
## Description
While developing the [improved Follow-Me](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/19260), **it was spotted that 2 follow-me messages were getting received roughly 0.1 seconds apart. The expected behavior is a steady 1 Hz message received**, therefore it raised speculation that MAVSDK is sending 2 messages around the same time.

The Message Burst behavior is shown below, with a **vertical (infinite derivative) plot of data points in Follow-Me messages begin received.** Indicating that they were published around the same time by MAVSDK (burst-published)

![BothVelTest_Screenshot from 2022-04-28 09-59-04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23277211/165715904-38fd4e3b-014b-40c7-8070-381c787d2b23.png)

## Ways to reproduce
1. Clone the Follow-Me MAVSDK script : https://github.com/junwoo091400/px4-follow-me-sim
2. Follow the instructions of README to install dependencies (which will install MAVSDK v1.2.0 in virtual environment for python)
3. Fetch and checkout the branch that I am developing on : https://github.com/junwoo091400/PX4-Autopilot/tree/followme_refactor
4. Run the SITL with the branch in step.3 : `make px4_sitl gazebo HEADLESS=1 `
5. Run the script in the px4-follow-me-sim repo from step.1 : `python3 follow-target-sim.py --model go_and_stop`
6. Wait for script to run ~ 30 seconds
7. Open the log of SITL with a PlotJuggler
8. Plot the 'follow_target' message logged. It will have vertical plot points like shown above.

### Logs
[MAVSDK_FollowMe_burst_messages.zip](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/8581318/MAVSDK_FollowMe_burst_messages.zip)
* It holds 2 logs where I tested the procedure above with MAVSDK v1.2.0 and v0.22.0 individually.

## Few Notes
1. There was a fix for a similar (potentially the same) issue 1 year ago : #1405 
2. However the **symptom happens both when using the MAVSDK v1.12.0 (Only a month old) and v0.22.0 (3 years old) - *image attached below**. Even though the Fix PR was added in between :thinking: 
3. The burst-sending happens only from time to time (irregularly)

Here, the left side is a SITL result of using MAVSDK v1.12.0 and right is using v0.22.0:
![LeftMAVSDKv1 12 0_Rightv0 22 0_Screenshot from 2022-04-28 10-47-03](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23277211/165717645-2af8ed76-e6a4-4eee-856f-8097dd36802a.png)

title: `set_root_directory()` does not set the root directory (FTP)
body:
The [`set_root_directory`](http://mavsdk-python-docs.s3-website.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/plugins/ftp.html#mavsdk.ftp.Ftp.set_root_directory) function is supposed to update the local root directory for the FTP service by updating `_root_dir` in `MavlinkFtp`.

I added `LogWarn() << "_root_dir: " << _root_dir;` to the `_work_list()` function and it still prints the default value of `_root_dir` (which is `.`) even after calling `set_root_directory`.

**To reproduce:** The easiest thing is to run the FTP server example (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/examples/ftp_server/ftp_server.cpp) and try passing in different root directories. No matter what you pass in, the root directory will always be set to the current working directory (i.e. `.`, the default value of `_root_dir`).

Big thanks for @julianoes for helping me work through this and some other FTP issues.

I'm guessing this is going to be a simple fix, but I can't see the issue and Julian hasn't had time, so I'm making this issue in the hopes that someone else might see what's going wrong.

title: Unsupported Mission Commands from QGroundcontrol created mission
body:
Hi MAVSDK Team,

Any mission created from QGroundcontrol throws "UNSUPPORTED mission item" error for few of the MAVLink Commands (MAV_CMD). 
QGC mission creation adds the following MAV_CMD commands to the mission plan by default unless unchecked

1. MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF ([22](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF) )
2. MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_MODE ([530](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_SET_CAMERA_MODE) )

When Download Mission api is called MAVSDK throws error which can be seen on mavsdk server console

```

[04:36:45|Debug] Assembling Message: 0 (mission_impl.cpp:612)
[04:36:45|Error] UNSUPPORTED mission item command (530) (mission_impl.cpp:743)
```

Looking at `DownloadMissionCallback` of `mission_impl.cpp` these commands are not part of the if else condition. Could you please confirm if there is a reason these have been left out? Is there any workaround to fix the UNSUPPORTED error on download mission?

I tested the new RTK plugin and it works like a charm ! Thank you @julianoes for the job.

In my working setup I have something like this:

title: Why no mavsdk-windows-x64-release.zip in latest version?
Use 2 UDP ports for sending and receiving data
body:
Hello,

I am wondering if it is possible to setup mavsdk with a UDP connection where messages are received on one localhost::udp tuple and sent to another localhost::udp tuple.

Quick explainer: the method we used to go with in OpenHD has always been: 
On the ground unit,
1) listen for messages from the Ground controll application on one udp localhost port
2) send messages to the ground controll application on another udp localhost port.

So for example, the ground controll application listens on localhost::16550 and sends data to localhost::16551

However, I cannot see a way to configure mavsdk to listen and send to different udp ports.
Since the send udp port is automatically added by using the address and port of a received packet.

Best regards, 
Constantin

title: Supporting SMART_BATTERY_INFO
body:
I got a request to expose the `serial_number` of [SMART_BATTERY_INFO](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#SMART_BATTERY_INFO).

From the specs, I read:

> Smart Battery information (static/infrequent update). Use for updates from: smart battery to flight stack, flight stack to GCS. Use [BATTERY_STATUS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#BATTERY_STATUS) for smart battery frequent updates.

Should I try to integrate that to the normal `Battery` updates of MAVSDK (I guess setting `serial_number=""` for non-smart batteries), or should it go in a specific `SmartBattery` type that comes with another subscription?

@hamishwillee @julianoes I wanted to ask for your opinion on that :slightly_smiling_face:.

Related to https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/290

title: Offboard integration tests don't realise offboard is active
body:
Seems to me that [those](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/integration_tests/offboard_velocity.cpp#L78) [tests](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/integration_tests/offboard_acceleration.cpp#L66) often fail here:

```
// Let's make sure that offboard knows it is active.
EXPECT_TRUE(offboard->is_active());
```

I am not sure if it is a problem in the test (should we remove that `EXPECT_TRUE`?) or if we have a bug.

But looking at the code, e.g. [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/db81f5cab44d6b521cc77a8979501da36128ca65/src/mavsdk/plugins/offboard/offboard_impl.cpp#L194), I don't see how it could _not_ be "active" after [the call of set_velocity_ned](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/integration_tests/offboard_velocity.cpp#L72) has been called like hundreds of times :thinking:.

I'm a bit confused :sweat_smile:. @julianoes any idea?

title: Add .proto files to release archives
body:
I downloaded mavsdk-windows-x64-release v1.4.3 for mavsdk_server and realized the .proto files need to be retrieved separately from a different repository. This also seems to apply to the .deb and .rpm releases. Since mavsdk_server is a gRPC server and a client cannot interact with it without the schema, it would be great to have the .proto files available as part of the release.

In this case I just wanted to try the server with [grpcui](https://github.com/fullstorydev/grpcui), but there are other use cases like running similar tools (gRPCurl, ghz, etc.) or generating code for a language that is not supported yet.

On a side note, it would also help to somehow note the version / commit hash of the MAVSDK-Proto repository used in the release.

Thanks!

title: Serial port connection to PX4 SITL not working with MAVSDK v1.4.4 after upgrading to latest PX4 firmware v1.3.0
body:
After upgrading one of our Cube Orange PX4 Flight Controllers from PX4 firmware Stable Release v1.12.3 to v1.3.0 MAVSDK v1.4.4 (running on Windows 11 operating system compiled with Visual Studio 2022) is not able to establish a serial connection (i.e. serial://COM16:57600) with the autopilot. It does work when using UDP connection. There is a workaround for it which is to first start QGroundControl and close it down, then connect to the same serial port via MAVSDK. As soon as the autopilot is restarted MAVSDK fails to connect again via serial port until QGroundControl has been run once on the same serial port. The issue has been tested on 2 different flight controllers running SITL. Both tested with my own MAVSDK based software as well with the "fly_mission.cpp" example under MAVSDK GitHub.
![MAVSDK_fail_to_connect_to_serial_port](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69586779/185954905-77dec52c-e91e-4dc9-a692-7844f5e3da47.jpg)

title: in MAVSDK/examples/fly_mission/fly_mission.cpp
[Discussion] How to set a parameter and reboot the vehicle for PX4 MAVSDK SITL Test
body:
## What I want to do
I wanted to have the following feature on [MAVSDK Test](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/tree/main/test/mavsdk_tests) in PX4 SITL:
1. Set the parameter in PX4 (to set it to a non-default value)
2. Reboot the vehicle (Or start the vehicle directly with the modified parameter from the beginning)
3. Perform a SITL MAVSDK test with the vehicle that had the modified parameter when it booted up

The reason for this was for the [Payload delivery SITL test PR](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/20230), I needed a way to set the parameter and reboot the vehicle, in order to have the startup script recognize the non-default parameter to enable the `payload_deliverer` module, and start the module, which is necessary for payload delivery feature.

## Problem
Currently it seems like we can't arbitrarily set the parameter before booting up, neither can we reboot the vehicle in the SITL test function.

### Proposed Solutions
1. Have a way to reboot the vehicle after setting the parameter in the mavsdk sitl test pipeline
2. Have a way to load an arbitrary / modified parameter through MAVSDK interface for the drone

## Discussion 
If we want to support such feature, what would be the best way to implement it? Are there any other solutions? Would this be possible without modifying MAVSDK?
