title: Provided MAVLink headers are installed to the wrong directory
body:
When supplying MAVLink C-header files and building from source, the build system installs the headers to a location that's not able to be found by `mavlink_include.h`.

Ubuntu 18.04 LTS
CMake v3.24.3

Configuration:
`cmake -B build/default -S . -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=all -DMAVLINK_HEADERS=../my_headers -H.`

Build and Install:
`sudo cmake --build build/default --target install -j8`

Resulting directory structure:
`/usr/local/include/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/**my_headers**/mavlink/v2.0/...`

Include line from `mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_include.h`:
`#include "mavlink/v2.0/all/mavlink.h`

---

To fix this, I edited `mavsdk/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/CMakeLists.txt`:
```
install(DIRECTORY
    ${MAVLINK_HEADERS} --> ${MAVLINK_HEADERS}/mavlink
    DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough
)
```

---

Please let me know if I'm doing something incorrectly. If I'm not, please update that `install(...)` command in the next release. Thanks! :)

title: REQUEST_MESSAGE vs custom getters like REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION
body:
It's currently part of the [list for MAVSDK v2](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2002), and though I don't think I can contribute an implementation, I think I can contribute a (relatively informed) opinion.

TL;DR: I don't think this can go in MAVSDK v2 :see_no_evil:.

#### We cannot detect what the receiver supports

There is no way to detect if the receiver supports `REQUEST_MESSAGE`, because the requested message could have been requested by someone else, or it could be transmitted spontaneously by the receiver. So making statistics to try to guess stuff like "was this `CAMERA_INFORMATION` message an answer to my request, or is it a coincidence?" is probably not worth it by far.

Also each message is independent. So even if we managed to detect that `REQUEST_MESSAGE` is supported for `CAMERA_INFORMATION`, it would not say anything about e.g. `REQUEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

#### What we can do

* Push the receivers to support both messages (i.e. the drone should support both `REQUEST_MESSAGE(<camera_information>)` and `REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION`.
* Keep the old way in MAVSDK until we feel like we can completely drop it.

In other words, the implementation work is not on the MAVSDK side, but on the receiver side (e.g. make sure that PX4/Ardupilot support the newer messages, make sure that cameras do, push proprietary players to do it).

Some day, maybe we will feel comfortable in dropping the old way and telling people "well if your drone does not support the new way, that's your problem".

title: UDP to remote port does not recognize disconnect
body: Configuring the mavsdk to `always_send_heartbeats` will properly send heartbeats to the simulator/vehicle, however [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/ea0b720538cff8e51947557234cb9c4300edadc3/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L536) sets the system to always consider itself as connected. So even though the mavsdk is sending heartbeats, if enough are missed to normally signal a disconnect, that disconnect is never recognized and any `subscribe_is_connected` callbacks on the system are not fired. I raised https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2074 to fix this issue.

title: Mavsdk::remove_connection does not remove system
body:
I believe there are still some subscriptions on the MAVSDK side for the removed connection. When removing and re-adding a connection, I get multiple printouts of messages (see heartbeat, MAVLink: info:, and Received ack messages in attached log).

It looks like the connection is removed, but the system itself is not. So when we reconnect we get duplicate messages.

At this point, I am not subscribed to anything but `subscribe_is_connected` (which is unsubscribed when a disconnect happens) and `subscribe_on_new_system` (which is unsubscribed when the connection is made). Unsubscribing everything on my end does not fix the multiple messages. For example, the only time I see `_heartbeat_timeout_cookie` ("heartbeats timed out" message) unsubscribed is when the `SystemImpl` is destructed, but `_systems` in `MavskImpl` is only cleared on destruction and I don't see any way to remove the system after removing the connection.

I found that the system id of my first system is changed to 1 in [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/ed7ac0777f97a84531c1790cbbc2b0de0438225b/src/mavsdk/core/mavsdk_impl.cpp#L356). However, subsequent connections (after disconnect of initial one and removal of connection) create systems with ID zero and are not changed to 1 because the systems list is not empty. Seems like we need to properly remove the systems - and all internal subscriptions to them - in order for it to properly remove and add a new remote system and have it work correctly.

If you point me to where exactly this filtering happens I could submit an MR.

title: Module range mismatch in "ActionImpl::set_actuator_async" function
body:
Hi,
I think I might have just found a minor bug in the ["set_actuator_async"](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L516) function.
The range in the switch...case statement goes from 1 to 6 while the range of the module function (index % 6) goes from 0 to 5.
So, param6 will never be set and if (index==6), then param7 will be equal to 1 and the whole command will be ignored by PX4 [handle_message_command_both](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/1c8ab2a0d7db2d14a6f320ebd8766b5ffaea28fa/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_receiver.cpp#L557) function.

If I understood correctly, at the moment PX4 only pays attention to 3 AUX outputs, namely param1, param2 and param3... so this bug should not have any effect on the whole system behavior.

title: FTP Server file descriptor leak
body:
**Version**: 1.4.16 as well as main

The FTP Server currently leaks a file descriptor every time MavlinkFtp::_work_list is called as it does not call closedir() on the descriptor used.

If there is a system limit for file descriptors, the server will eventually start failing to open any further descriptors. This was confirmed by watching "/proc/<pid>/fd" and observing errors when 1024 descriptors was reached.

This issue causes failures such as when requesting a directory listing, the client reports "Ftp::Result::ProtocolError" with the server reporting "OPC:CMD_OPEN_FILE_RO" followed by "FTP: Open failed"

Line where descriptor is allocated:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_ftp.cpp#L989

title: ArduPilot - Problem identified that may be causing the mission module to fail (fly_mission example)
body:
Hello, I have found a possible cause of this issue of the mission module failing in ArduPilot. 
Using Wireshark, I analyzed the network traffic between my ArduPilot SITL (running inside a WSL2 Docker container that runs the latest ArduPilot Docker image) and the MAVSDK example (running inside WSL2 as I was having issues running it in Windows 10). My MAVSDK library and my fly_mission binary were built in _debug_ mode using CMake through CMake Tools in VSCode (using VSCode WSL Remote session).

Here is my terminal output:  
![image](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/57928210/31595d2e-923d-4817-aeea-85eb264c2683)

There is a debug message saying the gimbal version is v1, and that the mission is unsupported.
Examining Wireshark, the last message sent before the MISSION_ACK message containing the MAV_MISSION_UNSUPPORTED payload was MAV_CMD_DO_MOUNT_CONFIGURE (204). 

When gimbal angles are defined in a mission_item, the gimbal version is verified: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L460
We then use the version above and send a version specific message containing the gimbal configuration. Below, we see that the unsupported message is sent if the gimbal version is assumed to be v1, as is the case in my console output:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1188-L1221

It appears that MAVSDK is not finding out the supported gimbal version. Gimbal v1 is deprecated in ArduPilot as of version 4.3. Wireshark shows that no GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION (280) messages were sent from the AP and no MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE (512) message from MAVSDK requesting the gimbal version was sent. The GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION message is what the gimbal module uses to set the gimbal version.

I propose the following two solutions. I think the latter is more inclusive to more ArduPilot versions but the former could be implemented quicker:
- default to v2 if ArduPilot is detected
- send a request for GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION if ArduPilot is detected

What do you all think?

title: ArduPilot - Possibility of using MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO instead of MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR
body:
Hello,

I've been messing around with the set-actuator example with my WSL2 ArduPilot SITL. I have seen that the set_actuator function is causing an unsupported message to appear in my terminal. Upon investigation of the source code: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L516-L550
I see that MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR is being used to only set _one_ actuator to a specific value. This command is unsupported in ArduPilot (indicated by it's absence in [this list](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/mavlink-other-commands.html#mav-cmds))

In theory, we could use MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO to accomplish what MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR is doing in ArduPilot.
However, I am not sure if MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR is supported in PX4 (https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/15281).

Would it be more preferable to change the set_actuator function to use MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO or to implement a switch statement that implements MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO if the AP is found to be using ArduPilot?
I could attempt to implement a case such as this: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L658-L670

title: Can't do goto_location or do_orbit with C++ SDK
body:
Hello,

i am having trouble with the C++ SDK. I am using v1.4.15 with PX4 sitl and gazebo garden.

Problem Description:
I can't command the x500 quadcopter to reposition neither to do orbits. I tried using the mavsdk::Action Plugin with goto_location() and do_orbit() as well as sending a CommandInt with the MavlinkPassthrough Plugin.
This causes the quadcopter to land immediately. However, the commands are submitted successfully and no error is being logged.
I also can see the messages and ACKs being sent when debugging with the wireshark lua-plugin.
Sending the commands manually with QGC does work as well as the Python example for do_orbit.

How to reproduce:
`make px4_sitl_default gz_x500`

To isolate the problem, i added this bit of code in the takeoff_and_land example, after the system has taken off and waited for a few seconds:

``` auto orbit_res = action.do_orbit(20.f, 2.f, mavsdk::Action::OrbitYawBehavior::HoldFrontToCircleCenter, 47.398036222362471, 8.5450146439425509, 2.5);
    std::cout << "Orbit_Res: " << orbit_res << std::endl;
    if(orbit_res == mavsdk::Action::Result::Success){
        sleep_for(seconds(30));
    }
```

The result is that do_orbit returns SUCCESS but the drone lands immediately.
A zipped flight log is attached.

Any help would be much appreciated!
[log_17_2023-8-18-23-08-13.ulg.zip](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/12384017/log_17_2023-8-18-23-08-13.ulg.zip)

title: Action->set_maximum_speed doesn't work with ArduPilot?
body: I can't get MAVSDK Action->set_maximum_speed to work with ArduPilot. Looking at the MAVSDK code, it is using `MAX_SPEED_PARAM `(which is actually `MPC_XY_CRUISE`) to control the maximum speed. But for ArduPilot the parameter controlling the maximum speed in at least Auto (waypoint) and Guided (with `MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION`) is `WPNAV_SPEED`. Also unless you set `RTL_SPEED`, the `WPNAV_SPEED` parameter will be used for that as well. Also tried sending the MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_SPEED command with passthrough but I couldn't get ArduPilot to react to my commands in Guide mode. So right now I use MAVSDK Param->set_param_float with `WPNAV_SPEED` as argument every time I want to change the speed in Auto and Guided flight modes (after calling `goto_location_async`) I'm not an ArduPilot expert so I might not got it 100% correct :-)

title: Building MAIN breaks Euler Angle Values - ArduCopter (Returns NaN but works in v1.4.16)
body:
Hello!

I have been following #2031 as I had the same issue with the `GUIDED mode`. I could not get a drone to take off without manually setting it to `GUIDED mode` first. Thankfully, this issue has been solved now, thanks dev team! 

I followed the suggestion of building `main` from source and that has worked nicely so thank you. Unfortunately however, my previously working eulerAngle telemetry gets are now broken/ only return NaN values.

As the title suggests, this issue is raised for ArduCopter (and Rover, Plane etc.) and *not* for PX4 (which I have tried `main` and it works fine).

This is the code I used:
```cpp
mavsdk::Telemetry::EulerAngle eulerAngle = telemetry->attitude_euler();
```
Using `main` I get the following results for euler angle params:
![Screenshot 2023-09-20 at 22 07 27](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/49697817/6e0744b4-0246-4c74-9e43-6165b9100c0e)

Using `v1.4.16`, I get the following results for euler angle params:
![Screenshot 2023-09-20 at 22 05 02](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/49697817/645fac70-3017-4c64-8ed8-8ff6c3902c0c)

I suspect there is some code change that needs to be modified back to the `v1.4.16` version?

Thanks for your help in advance!

title: unix_epoch_time subscription not working in C++ and Python
body:

I'm currently trying to sync time between an external application and my mavlink device in C++. To do this I'm trying to subscribe to the "unix_epoch_time" telemetry.
Sadly, the callback is never called. To explore the issue, I also created a simple python script to display the telemetry message:
```python
import asyncio
from mavsdk import System

async def run():
    # Connect to the MAVSDK system
    system = System(mavsdk_server_address='localhost', port=50051)
    await system.connect()

    await system.telemetry.set_rate_unix_epoch_time(1)
    # Subscribe to time updates
```

title: When multiple vehicles are connected, all systems get data from all vehicles, regardless of sysid.
heap-use-after-free after heartbeats timed out when using UDP connection
body:
# tl;dr

This appears to be a timing issue and the application typically crashes at intermittent intervals. Shared or overused compute clusters can cause delays to network traffic (especially with a cloud-based simulation). Without directly observing a packet capture, this is a proposed sequence of events to reproduce in a regression test:
- connect over udp
- stop sending heartbeats
- get notified of disconnect
- immediately send gimbal events
- crash

# Description
This is observed with [mavsdk 7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da) when compiled with Address Sanitizer.

mavsdk library is used by a DroneUp application, the `mavlink_shim` and the whole application is built in a Docker-based workflow. We see a heap-use-after-free error which we believe is related to mavsdk and UDP network connectivity. The issue's reproducibility is intermittent -- we don't see it frequently nor for every heartbeats timed out event. Debugging an intermittent issue is difficult :rofl: 

We observe these events:
- our `mavlink_client` object is using mavsdk. It's configured to use a udp connection and has successfully connected.
- At some point, mavsdk reports a connection loss (eg, missed heartbeats)
- We then observe a crash in the gimbal manager inside of mavsdk
- The crash appears to be within mavsdk's internal components.


The crash provides the following stack trace information.

2. _mavsdk's **internal event thread**_ destroyed a `GimbalProtocolBase` object during continued notifications of the disconnected status.

    2. `heartbeats_timed_out()` calls `set_disconnected()` [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L268-L272)
    3. `set_disconnected()` notifies us (so we see a log message first) and then it disables all of the plugins [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L599-L623)

3. _mavsdk's **internal socket thread**_ tried to use that `GimbalProtocolBase` object after it had been freed, and crashed the application.
    1. A gimbal message is processed through the deleted `GimbalProtocolV2` and crashes in `process_gimbal_manager_status()` [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da/src/mavsdk/plugins/gimbal/gimbal_protocol_v2.cpp#L21-L53).
    2. It was captured with an unsynchronized `this` [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da/src/mavsdk/plugins/gimbal/gimbal_protocol_v2.cpp#L289-L291) for the callback.
    3. The function pointer is assigned a value [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7fe1b6083545a0760dc306388ea946ded78316da/src/mavsdk/plugins/gimbal/gimbal_protocol_v2.cpp#L21-L53) during asynchronous gimbal control.

UDP, being connectionless, still processes received datagrams even though the _event thread_ is handling a disconnect event and deletes things that the _socket thread_ needs for continued processing.

title: how to get Ardupilot Camera Trigger status?
Mission Upload issues with Mavsdk Java and Ardupilot
body:
In an effort to build capabilities while testing and learning mavsdk I have been modifying some of the example code in MavSDK Java to talk with a SITL Arducopter drone.

My Environment:
	- Windows 11 host
	- Ardupilot SITL using WSL Linux ubuntu
	- Mavsdk server from [Releases](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v2.0.0/mavsdk_server_musl_x86_64) hosted in Alpine 3.19 docker
	-  MavSDKJava examples running from intellij gradle task

The Issue:
When attempting to start a mission upload using the code snippet below I get a "TIMEOUT" return after just a second or 2. This error happens regardless of using MissionRaw or Mission plugins.

To Reproduce:
	- run mavsdk server  v2.0 using `./mavsdk_server --sysid 10 --compid 10 udp://:14450  -p 50051`
	- Install or otherwise have ardupilot SITL on your machine
	-  add `MCTSSA=33.246358,-117.425353,200,90` to your location.txt file located at `ardupilot/Tools/autotest/`
	- run the SITL using: `sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map --location MCTSSA --instance 0`
	- Manually give your drone a mission of fly-to points using the draw or edit features in MavProxy or otherwise get a mission to the drone
	- pull MavSDK-Java latest
	- Add [uploadIssueCode.txt](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/13923609/uploadIssueCode.txt) in `examples/java-client/src/main/java/io/mavsdk/example/` as a .java file
	- Run the file changing IS_RAW flag to true or false to change plugin used

I get times out on the request very quickly (1-2 seconds) with no log messages in Mavsdk.

SITL displays 
```
Got MISSION_ACK: TYPE_MISSION: OPERATION_CANCELLED
AP: Mission upload timeout:
```
sometime later about 10+ seconds after request

<details>

```cpp

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.15)

find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)

# Add executable target with source files
add_executable(telemetry-stream main.cpp)

# Link MAVSDK library
target_link_libraries(telemetry-stream
  MAVSDK::mavsdk
)
```

</details>

<details>

```
MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry
```

According to [this documentation](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/telemetry.html), `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry` is needed within the `target_link_libraries` call.

However, I wanted to ask: why there is a discrepancy between the documentation and the example, and which I should follow?

title: Server plugin should not receive commands that are addressed to other components.
body:
Hi!

I'm working on multiple cameras using [mavlink camera protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/camera.html) as it is [not supported so far](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_camera.html).

While browsing the source code I've noticed, that it seems the **component_id** field is missing in MAVLinkCommandIntHandlerTableEntry and MAVLinkCommandLongHandlerTableEntry which may be used to filter out commands sent to another component in a system (in a similar way as it is implemented for mavlink_message_handler)

As for now every camera server will process and react to all commands regardless if the component ID matches its own_component_id. For example, if I select camera and subscribe to video_stream_info - all cameras will send ack and video_stream_info message, which seems wrong to me.
This may be simply fixed as it is done [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/30825da62876b8437a9c06f11fe6ad77d79c8136/src/mavsdk/plugins/tracking_server/tracking_server_impl.cpp#L316):
But I'm not sure if this is the right place/level where it has to be done.

Many thanks!

Best regards,
Alex

title: Getting HTTP 503 when attempting to subscribe to telemetry but works after connecting with QGroundControl
body:
When I connect with `mavsdk_server_bin` to my drone running `ArduPilot`, I cannot subscribe for telemetry as my web client is receiving 503 from `mavsdk_server_bin`. It is the same behavior with `APM Planner` and I connect through the serial port in both cases(`mavsdk_server_bin` and `APM Planner`) mutually exclusively.

Once I connect with `QGroundControl` through the serial port, all the data starts streaming. From there on I can connect with either `APM Planner` or `mavsdk_server_bin` and they both receive the data just fine; and my web client can subscribe to telemetry just fine through `mavsdk_server_bin`.

I am not sure what triggers the data to start streaming through `QGroundControl `and I would expect this to be the norm to be honest. I am wondering if there is an `ArduPilot` setting to have this behavior enabled by default for all clients connecting to `mavlink` through serial/tcp/udp?

If I hardware reset the `ArduPilot` the same problem comes up as I need to run `QGroundControl` which somehow triggers the `mavlink` streaming.

APM-Planner v2-2.0.30-rc3
QGrountControl v4.3.0
MAVSDK-Server v2.9.1

Thank you!

title: Improve list_directory API
body: I want to change the API of `FTP::list_directory()` to give you a list of files and directories separately instead of having these odd prefixes `D` or `F`.

title: Adding Home Position Mavlink Message to Telemetry
body:
Currently, the [`subcribe_home` function](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_telemetry.html#classmavsdk_1_1_telemetry_1ae57e4c8741ba7ae05961cadfabc82875) in Telemetry API  returns a HomeHandle that uses the position struct which is in terms of global GPS position.

However, there is a mavlink message that gives more information about the [home position ](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HOME_POSITION)

In future releases, it would be much better to implement this mavlink message into mavsdk

title: Change RTK to base64
body:
Instead of using a string for the (binary) RTCMv3 corrections, I want to change this to a base64 encoded string.

This would be the same as it's done in [LogStreaming](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/572d28d6c30dc59448427e84ce9a7301c534e80a/src/mavsdk/plugins/log_streaming/include/plugins/log_streaming/log_streaming.h#L65).

title: Switch to clearer API for UDP and TCP
body:
The way that `udp://:port` means "listen" and `udp://IP:port` means "send to IP" often causes confusion and frustration.

I suggest we adopt [the way it's done in pymavlink](https://mavlink.io/en/mavgen_python/#connection_string).

We can leave the current way to be backwards compatible.

Opinions @JonasVautherin ?

title: MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS: Sigfault when multiple IN_PROGRESS messages are sent before arming
body:
Drone Device: Skydio X2

When sending arming commands to the Skydio X2, it performs a long warm-up routine.
While the warm-up routine is running, MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS messages are sent.
When the drone is finished warming up it returns a MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED message.

This state flow is represented in MAVSDK/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.cpp.

Whenever the second MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS is sent, I get a Sigfault from mavsdk.
It occurs when freeing the memory of a promise. 
 
The "call_callback(temp_callback, temp_result.first, temp_result.second);" function inside  
"MavlinkCommandSender::receive_command_ack(mavlink_message_t message)" is the start of the error stack.  

Does the dev team have any drones that return MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS messages before success when arming?
Is this an expected working feature. 
The workflow does not work for the Skydio X2.

Inside MAVSDK/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.cpp:
All other case statement flows remove the job from the queue: "_work_queue.erase(it)"
Likely, any job that reaches the call_callback function twice will cause a Sigfault. 
The only jobs able to go through the case statement twice are jobs that are returned a PROGRESS message.

Current mitigation: Disabling call_callback for any Progress message. 
Mavlink seems to work perfectly fine with call_callback disabled for Progress message, must not be used anywhere crucial. 

```
        if (temp_callback != nullptr) {
            if (temp_result.first != Result::InProgress)
            {
                call_callback(temp_callback, temp_result.first, temp_result.second);
            }
        }
```

title: How do you use `telemetry_server` correctly?
body:
I have the following code that reads a CSV over the network with telemetry I want to feed to PX4:

```python
import asyncio
import io
import csv
import numpy as np
from functools import partial
from typing import Dict, Any
from decimal import Decimal
from mavsdk import System
from mavsdk.telemetry_server import (
    Position, VelocityNed, Heading, Imu,
    AccelerationFrd, AngularVelocityFrd, MagneticFieldFrd
)

G_CONSTANT = 9.80665
ACCEL_DATA_G = []
TIME_INTERVAL = 1 / 30 # We're sampling at 30Hz

async def send_telemetry(drone: System, data: Dict[Any,Any]):
    global ACCEL_DATA_G

    ACCEL_DATA_G.append(
        [
            float(data['accelerometerAccelerationX(G)']),
            float(data['accelerometerAccelerationY(G)']),
            float(data['accelerometerAccelerationZ(G)'])
        ]
    )

    accel_data_g = np.array(ACCEL_DATA_G)
    accel_data_m_s2 = accel_data_g * G_CONSTANT
    velocity = np.zeros_like(accel_data_m_s2)

    for i in range(1, len(accel_data_m_s2)):
        velocity[i] = velocity[i-1] + (accel_data_m_s2[i-1] + accel_data_m_s2[i]) / 2 * TIME_INTERVAL

    average_velocity = np.mean(velocity, axis=0)
    #print(f"Velocity in m/s (NED): {average_velocity}")

    await drone.telemetry_server.publish_position(
        position=Position(
            latitude_deg=float(data['locationLatitude(WGS84)']),
            longitude_deg=float(data['locationLongitude(WGS84)']),
            absolute_altitude_m=float(data['locationAltitude(m)']),
            relative_altitude_m=float(data['altimeterRelativeAltitude(m)'])
        ),
        velocity_ned=VelocityNed(
            north_m_s=average_velocity[0],
            east_m_s=average_velocity[1],
            down_m_s=average_velocity[2]
        ),
        heading=Heading(
            heading_deg=float(data['locationTrueHeading(°)'])
        )
    )

    """
    #drone.telemetry_server.publish_imu()
    await drone.telemetry_server.publish_raw_imu(
        Imu(
            acceleration_frd=AccelerationFrd(
                forward_m_s2=float(data['accelerometerAccelerationX(G)']),
                right_m_s2=float(data['accelerometerAccelerationY(G)']),
                down_m_s2=float(data['accelerometerAccelerationZ(G)'])
            ),
            angular_velocity_frd=AngularVelocityFrd(
                forward_rad_s=float(data['gyroRotationX(rad/s)']),
                right_rad_s=float(data['gyroRotationY(rad/s)']),
                down_rad_s=float(data['gyroRotationZ(rad/s)'])
            ),
            magnetic_field_frd=MagneticFieldFrd(
                forward_gauss=float(Decimal(data['motionMagneticFieldX(µT)']) / Decimal(100)), # 1 Gauss is equal to 100 µT
                right_gauss=float(Decimal(data['motionMagneticFieldY(µT)']) / Decimal(100)),
                down_gauss=float(Decimal(data['motionMagneticFieldZ(µT)']) / Decimal(100))
            ),
            temperature_degc=0,
            timestamp_us=int(float(data['locationTimestamp_since1970(s)'])) * 1_000_000
        )
    )
    """

async def handle_echo(reader, writer, drone: System):
    addr = writer.get_extra_info('peername')
    print(f"Received connection from {addr}")

    fields = None

    with open('telem.csv', 'w') as f:
        while True:
            data = await reader.readline()
            message = data.decode()
            #addr = writer.get_extra_info('peername')
            #print(f"Received connection from {addr}")
            #print(message)
            f.write(message)

            if 'loggingTime' in message:
                fields = message.strip().split(',')
                print(message)
                continue

            buf = io.StringIO(message)
            csv_reader = csv.DictReader(buf, fieldnames=fields)

            for row in csv_reader:
```

title: Disable automatically re-sending setpoints in offboard
body:
Is there a way to disable the MAVSDK offboard class from automatically re-sending setpoints?

It seems that this is done to bypass the fact that Px4 needs off-board setpoints to be minimally sent at 2Hz, however there is a good reason Px4 does that. 
The current behaviour of MAVSDK can leave the drone mindlessly following the last setpoint if there is an unexpected fault on the companion computer. This is particularly a problem with velocity setpoints.

I guess I could modify the value of SEND_INTERVAL_S, but that seems like a less than optimal solution.

title: TCP connection from MAVSDK breaks app after 16 minutes of idle time due to reconnection
body:
I'm developing an app that uses MAVSDK to connect to a device via the built-in MAVSDK TCP connection. MAVSDK has an excellent TCP reconnection mechanism that fits my requirements well, namely the possibility of temporary disconnection. In this case timer is started, which checks every second whether the connection has been restored. But after 16 minutes, this mechanism breaks my app with the message **"socket errorToo many open files"**. 

I did some basic research and the problem is that the MAVSDK in a loop reopens the sockets, but does not close them with the `close` function in case of unsuccessful execution of the `connect` function. 

```
// from tcp_connection.cpp

_socket_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
```

I have tested basic fix on Linux, but I don't know if it will work on other operating systems

title: QUESTION: I noticed MavSDK initiates 4 MavlinkMessageHandler when connecting using MavSDK-JAVA. Why does MavSDK initiates 4 handlers to handle MavLink messages? Are there any reasons for this approach?
Simplify build process
body:
**Issue**
It's not super easy to build the library, and I'm not sure how to do a clean build without removing the dependencies added via FetchContent. It would be nice to be able to remove only the source build files so that we don't have to always redownload the dependencies (right now I just delete build/ and install/)

**Solution**
For my C++ projects I always add a Makefile to wrap the CMake commands. I like doing this because for every project I know I can run `make`, `make clean` and `make install`. The underlying actions of each recipe could vary, but it makes it easy for me to switch between projects without having to remember specifics of how they're built/deployed.

```cmake
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)

project(mavsdk_takeoff)

find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)

add_executable(main main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(main  MAVSDK::mavsdk MAVSDK::mavsdk_action)
```

title: Disconnection Issue with Ardupilot Flight Controller on serial port
body: The C++ mavsdk-based onboard computer program connects to the Ardupilot flight controller through Telem2. After establishing the connection, the flight controller will automatically disconnect after a random duration. Later, through the serial port debugging tool, I found that the flight controller’s Telem2 port had no MAVLink data stream output. However, after restarting the flight controller software using Mission Planner (MP), data returned and the connection was re-established correctly (I ruled out hardware issues through this). Once the serial port detects that the flight controller has disconnected, even if I restart my control program, it still cannot reconnect. I later tried using a TCP/UDP connection to the flight controller, but the disconnection issue persisted. However, sometimes after about half an hour, the flight controller reconnects on its own. This issue has been bothering me for months. I want to know why the flight controller serial port behaves this way. From the Ardupilot wiki, I learned that there may be conflicts caused by telemetry link sharing, but I am not sure if this is the cause of the problem, since I also use Telem1 to connect to QGC. I would greatly appreciate it if anyone could help me analyze the possible causes.

title: cmakelists对交叉编译的支持有问题
body:
在third_party/cmake/build_target.cmake 内  缺少对 CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME  CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR  CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING 这三个参数的读取 应该加上这三行 
"-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=${CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME}"
 "-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR}"
"-DCMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING=${CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING}"



那么完整的应该如下

execute_process(
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND}
            "-G${CMAKE_GENERATOR}"
            "${PLATFORM_ARGUMENT}"
            "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=${CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE}"
            "-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE:PATH=${CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE}"
            "-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=${TARGET_INSTALL_DIR}"
            "-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH:PATH=${CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH}"
            "-DPLATFORM=${PLATFORM}" # for iOS toolchain
            "-DDEPLOYMENT_TARGET=${DEPLOYMENT_TARGET}" # for iOS toolchain
            "-DENABLE_STRICT_TRY_COMPILE=${ENABLE_STRICT_TRY_COMPILE}" # for iOS toolchain
            "-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=${CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME}"
            "-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR}"
            "-DCMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING=${CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING}"
            "-DMAVLINK_DIALECT=${MAVLINK_DIALECT}"
            "${TARGET_SOURCE_DIR}"
        WORKING_DIRECTORY "${TARGET_BINARY_DIR}"
        RESULT_VARIABLE CONFIGURE_FAILED
    )

title: RC_Status and mavlink remote health
body:
MAVSDK `RcStatus` will return `is_available = False` while autopilot has can't be armed

[PX4 manualControlCheck.cpp](https://github.com/aminballoon/PX4-Autopilot/blob/v1.15.0-alpha1/src/modules/commander/HealthAndArmingChecks/checks/manualControlCheck.cpp)

In this case if **Kill switch engaged** *RCStatus::is_available will be False** by this Flag


[RC_OK Flag check](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2304566ad9d1b7aa98bf0f12baee5f7151613589/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp#L1029-L1030C87) ``` const bool rc_ok = sys_status.onboard_control_sensors_health & MAV_SYS_STATUS_SENSOR_RC_RECEIVER; ```

In my opinion, when the kill switch is engaged, it doesn't mean that the RC is not available; it's available, but it just can't be armed.

The `rc_ok` Flag should not be check only MAV_SYS_STATUS_SENSOR_RC_RECEIVER or I need to contribute manualControlCheck in PX4 . 

I can add proto [Mavlink RC_CHANNELS_RAW](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#:~:text=UINT8_MAX%3A%20invalid/unknown.-,RC_CHANNELS_RAW,-(35)) for check the latest RC input by Timestamp and solve this issue.
What do you think about this issue and my solution ?

body:
Error during confiugration:
```sh
cmake -S . -B buld
```

with result:
```sh
[100%] Built target mavlink
CMake Warning:
  Ignoring empty string ("") provided on the command line.


CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:1 (cmake_minimum_required):
  Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.

  Update the VERSION argument <min> value.  Or, use the <min>...<max> syntax
  to tell CMake that the project requires at least <min> but has been updated
  to work with policies introduced by <max> or earlier.

  Or, add -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 to try configuring anyway.


-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
CMake Error at third_party/cmake/build_target.cmake:32 (message):
  
  /mnt/zyncdev/user/NovaLabs/Hammer/repos/mavlink/mavlink-tools/mavsdk/third_party/jsoncpp
  failed to configure!
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  third_party/CMakeLists.txt:12 (build_target)


-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
```

Sounds like `third_party/jsoncpp/CMakeLists.txt` just should be updated to point to the cmake 3.5 at least. But I suggest change it to the same minimum cmake version, that used for root CMakeLists.txt for now: 3.13.

Same suggestion for all other third_party components, that point to the cmake 3.1.

Also, jsoncpp must be updated itself. It provides `src/jsoncpp/jsoncppConfig.cmake.in` that points into CMake 3.0 policy. Newest version updates it: https://github.com/open-source-parsers/jsoncpp/blob/master/jsoncppConfig.cmake.in

Another solution, just set ENV variable `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` at the top-level CMakeLists.txt:
```cmake
set(ENV{CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM} 3.13)
```
or run configuration like:
```sh
env CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.16 cmake -S . -B buld
```

title: Windows 11 dependencies not found
body:
I have tried both building the mavsdk library from source and using the generated one (zip file with the build artifacts). There are numerous issues and this is not an exhaustive list:

**1. The windows default app python does not work with the build: it must be uninstalled and a newer one installed from python.org**

**2. When configuring the build (`cmake -Bbuild -S.`), there is some a missing dependency:**
- Perl: can be installed via an msi installer package

**3. When building the mavsdk libraries from source, I followed the CI containers method by using:**
```
cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" $env:superbuild -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$PWD/build/release/third_party/install" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=build/release/install -DBUILD_MAVSDK_SERVER=ON -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DWERROR=ON -Bbuild/release -S.
```

->Otherwise there are a lot of linker errors when using the [recommended cmake](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build.html#release) command for windows


**4. When linking to the generated mavsdk libraries cmake can not find curl (and by extension tinyxml2, jsoncpp, grpc).** Basically the dependencies in MAVSDKConfig.cmake are not found because they aren't installed to where cmake can find them in the base MAVSDK directory.

**5. There is a warning for windows to build with a local install in the Building C++ apps guide of the mavsdk docs, but this should explicitly say that system wide install is not supported.**

If this is the user experience for trying to develop on windows, can we really say it is supported or should there be an "at your own risk" warning?

title: how to control the motor directly?
Issue of Mission Execution and Manual Input Priority
body:
When the "manual_control.set_manual_control_input"s value keeps changing, I want to execute a mission or other automode. In such a case, the value needs to remain consistent before and after the mission is triggered; otherwise, the mission will be interrupted. However, I’ve noticed that even if I set the manual value right before executing the mission, and then immediately trigger the task, it still gets interrupted. It turns out that I have to wait several hundred milliseconds after setting the value before executing the mission. It seems that the mission has a higher priority, even if the command is input later, the flight controller receives and processes it first.

Then I looked into the source code and found that these two types of commands follow different paths，one goes through a queue, while the other is sent directly as a command. So now I’m wondering: how can I make the information in the queue be delivered faster, so that I don’t have to wait for several hundred milliseconds?

Im current using v3.3.0
Thanks.

title: UDP reconnect logic with PX4
body:
I think this issue has probably caught a few people out in the past. But when using UDP with PX4, PX4 will record the port & ip address of the first heartbeat it receives. It will then send any status and responses to this address. This address is set once, and only once, and so if you disconnect and reconnect with a different local port (on client), you will not receive any messages until the PX4 is rebooted.

Suggest adding a default port to MavSDK which it attempts to bind to, currently it is set to 0 so OS picks a 'sensible' random port.

title: Double Unlock in LockedQueue::Guard
body:
## Problem

- The `LockedQueue::Guard` class locks the mutex in constructor and unlocks in destructor
- `wait_and_pop_front()` manually unlocks the mutex, then re-locks with `unique_lock`
- When the method returns, both the `unique_lock` and `Guard` get destroyed as they leave scope
- The `unique_lock` destructor AND `Guard` destructor try to unlock the same mutex
- This causes undefined behavior (double-unlock) that can crash/hang the program

Personally I experienced this causing indefinite hangs in my application.

## History

- First observed in v3.7.0 release
- Does not reproduce in v3.6.0 release
- Likely introduced in commit https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/commit/1abe3ea074e3c340d6c26865788a5980826a1c8e by @julianoes

title: How to send statustext message?
mavlink_direct: Message filtering not working in subscribe_message (v3.10.1)
body:
## Bug Description
The `mavlink_direct` plugin's `subscribe_message` method does not properly filter messages when a specific `message_name` is provided. Instead of receiving only the requested message type, subscribers receive ALL message types.

## Expected Behavior
When subscribing with a specific message name (e.g., `message_name="HEARTBEAT"`), the subscriber should only receive messages of that type.

## Actual Behavior
Subscribers receive ALL message types regardless of the filter specified. The `message_name` parameter is completely ignored.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start MAVSDK server v3.10.1
2. Connect via gRPC and use the mavlink_direct service
3. Call `SubscribeMessage` with `message_name="HEARTBEAT"`
4. Observe that you receive all message types (ATTITUDE, TIMESYNC, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.)

## Test Results
Testing with a Python gRPC client shows:
- **No filter (empty string)**: Correctly receives all 34 message types
- **Filter "HEARTBEAT"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive HEARTBEAT)
- **Filter "TIMESYNC"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive TIMESYNC)
- **Filter "ATTITUDE"**: Incorrectly receives all 34 message types (should only receive ATTITUDE)

## Root Cause Analysis
Looking at the code in `mavlink_direct_impl.cpp`:
- The `subscribe_message` method stores the `message_name` filter
- It registers with `SystemImpl::register_libmav_message_handler`
- However, when messages arrive, they're forwarded to ALL subscribers regardless of their individual filters
- The stored `message_name` is never actually used to filter messages before invoking callbacks

## Environment
- MAVSDK version: v3.10.1
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Connection: gRPC on port 50051
- Test vehicle: PX4 SITL

## Workaround
Until fixed, users must manually filter messages in their client code:
```python
# Subscribe to all messages (empty filter)
request = mavlink_direct_pb2.SubscribeMessageRequest(message_name="")
responses = stub.SubscribeMessage(request)

for response in responses:
    if response.HasField('message'):
        msg = response.message
        # Manual filtering
        if msg.message_name == "HEARTBEAT":
            # Process only HEARTBEAT messages
            process_message(msg)
```

## Impact
This bug makes the filtering feature completely non-functional, forcing all clients to receive and process all messages, which can significantly impact performance in high-frequency telemetry scenarios.

title: MavlinkPassthrough unable to receive DATA32 messages
body:
Hi all,

I'm having trouble using `mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough` to receive `DATA32` MAVLink messages (Message ID = 170).

**Setup**

- **Autopilot**: Onboard, running ArduPilot
- **Companion Computer**: Sends `DATA32` messages, uses **component ID 192**

**Problem**

The Companion sends `DATA32` messages, and I'm trying to catch them using the following code:

```
mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough m_passthrough;
m_passthrough.subscribe_message(170, [](const mavlink_message_t& message) {
          mavlink_data32_t data_msg;
          mavlink_msg_data32_decode(&message, &data_msg);

          std::cout << "Received DATA32 message " << std::endl;
}
```

However, the callback is **never triggered**.

**Debugging Attempts**

Initially, I suspected the issue might be related to the **component ID** (Companion uses 192). To test this, I subscribed to the `HEARTBEAT` message, and that **does work**:

```
m_passthrough.subscribe_message(MAVLINK_MSG_ID_HEARTBEAT, [](const mavlink_message_t& message) {
          mavlink_heartbeat_t heartbeat;
          mavlink_msg_heartbeat_decode(&message, &heartbeat);

          uint8_t sysid = message.sysid;   // System ID of the sender
          uint8_t compid = message.compid; // Component ID of the sender
          std::cout << "HEARTBEAT from sysid: " << static_cast<int>(sysid) << ", compid: " << static_cast<int>(compid) << "\n";
}
```

So I know messages from the Companion are being received.

**Validation from Python**

To confirm that the `DATA32` messages are being sent correctly, I used the following Python script (via `pymavlink`), and it does receive the messages:

```
from pymavlink import mavutil

# Create a connection listening on UDP port 14551
master = mavutil.mavlink_connection('udpin:0.0.0.0:14551')

print("Waiting for messages...")

while True:
    # Wait for the next message with a timeout of 1 second
    msg = master.recv_match(type=None, blocking=True, timeout=1)

    if msg is None:
        continue  # Timeout, no message received

    # Check if the message ID matches 170
    if msg.get_msgId() == 170:
        print("received")
```

This confirms that `DATA32` messages are sent and received with the correct payload.

I'm currently stuck. My gut feeling is that the issue might be related to `DATA32` not being part of the standard MAVLink protocol, but instead part of the ardupilotmega dialect.

I’ve searched around but haven’t found a definitive answer. So my questions are:

- Is t his a bug or known limitation in MavSDK?
- Does MavSDK's MavlinkPassthrough support custom or dialect-specific messages like `DATA32`?
- Is there a workaround or known approach to handle these messages correctly?

I’d really appreciate any help or guidance—I'm out of ideas at this point.

Thanks in advance!

All I see are the hard-coded set(MAVLINK_MINIMAL_XML... in the CMakeLists.txt and when I change these to point to my location, MAVSDK is built properly.

If, like @JonasVautherin suggested, there is a way to specify this location via a cmake flag, it would be fine I guess. Not sure how that should be done so I would like to ask you... thanks!

Update: ok, that wasn't so hard, created a PR to set the variables only when not specified

title: MavlinkDirect API doesn't seem to support uint64_t fields when they have large number
body:
MavlinkDirect API doesn't seem to support uint64_t fields when they have large number, for example GPS2_RAW message:
```
JSON: {"alt_ellipsoid":45358,"lat":201849905,"lon":108122620,"time_usec":1759841673570912}
[03:54:33|Warn ] Field time_usec is not a float or double field (mavlink_direct_impl.cpp:292)
```

title: sender/receiver based on MavlinkDirect working too slow
Gimbal device tester may fail if system under test consist of several components
body:
In case the system under test consists of several components i.e. send several Heartbeats (gimbal + camera, for ex.) [sysid_compid_correct check](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/examples/gimbal_device_tester/gimbal_device_tester.cpp#L679) may fail if the latest read Heartbeat was not from the gimabl device.

Proposed solution: In the Heartbeat message handler, check that message received from the gimbal device component.

title: Document/support process for using custom mavlink dialect
body:
I want to add a few custom mavlink messages for my own dialect, not part of upstream, and develop without having to commit and push to a repository.

Right now, mavlink is brought in through ExternalProject_add like so:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L32-L45



The URL is hard-coded to upstream
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L34

Then, for a local build, mavlink is built and installed, so that its config file is on disk.
This allows it to be found through find_package:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L4

For some reason, regardless of the setting for the MAVLINK_DIALECT, it does not get affect the command here:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L27-L39


I want to

* Add a new local mavlink XML dialect, say my_custom.xml
* Get MAVSDK to also generate that dialect in addition to the normal dialect
* Use those new messages to send custom packets via mavsdk

Can we either document or add support for mavlink to be brought in through a submodule, fetchcontent, or how to build/install mavlink on the system that does not rely on merging stuff upstream first? Perhaps we can support a way where mavlink on the system can be used.

In mavlink:
```
cmake -B build -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=MyCustomDialect
cmake --build build
cmake --install build --prefix install
```
Which generates the following header (as expected)
```
/home/ryan/Dev/mavlink/install/include/mavlink/MyCustomDialect/mavlink_msg_my_custom_dialect_toy.h
```
Then, when building MAVSDK, perhaps we can allow a user to add "/path/to/mavlink/install" to the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH and use that version instead of pulling from upstream.

Trying this today results in the following error:
```
gmake[2]: *** No rule to make target 'third_party/install/include/mavlink/message_definitions/v1.0/ardupilotmega.xml', needed by 'src/mavsdk/core/embedded_mavlink_xml.h'.  Stop.
gmake[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:910: src/mavsdk/core/CMakeFiles/generate_core_mavlink_xml_header.dir/all] Error 2
gmake: *** [Makefile:136: all] Error 2
```
I spent a fair bit of time trying to understand this step of the build system but don't know how to proceed.

title: Add euler quaternion conversion functions

CMake local install RPATH missing
body:
I tried consuming a locally installed version of MAVSDK in another package's install, and MAVSDK's CMake target fails to correctly export the shared library destination on an installed target.
I suspected this is an rpath issue, and spent 2 hours trying various recommendations, but have not found a solution.
Here is a conference talk from a CMake maintainer specifically about this use case with rpath:
https://youtu.be/m0DwB4OvDXk?si=3TaOFA6OdxY4z5F6&t=2452

I tried his recommendation on MAVSDK, and that did not fix the issue.

To reproduce, here's a Dockerfile:

```docker
FROM ubuntu:22.04

WORKDIR /ws

# https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build_linux.html

RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        python3 \
        python3-pip

RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
# Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install


RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        pkg-config \
        astyle \
        bluez \
        bluez-tools \
        libbluetooth-dev

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules --branch cmake-install https://github.com/ryanf55/RemoteIDTransmitter.git
WORKDIR /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter
RUN CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/ws/MAVSDK/install cmake -B build
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter
```

Just run `docker build . --progress=plain` and you will eventually get 
```
 > [stage-0 17/17] RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter:
0.378 ./install/bin/rid-transmitter: error while loading shared libraries: libmavsdk.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The example here is when I tried using an installed executable that links to MAVSDK.
The linkage to MAVSDK is using the standard target_link_libraries approach:
https://github.com/Ryanf55/RemoteIDTransmitter/blob/cmake-install/CMakeLists.txt#L37

title: Log file download resume after a partial download?
body:
Julian/Gents:
 I don't know if the community is interested in such a capability as it is sort of a unique situation. Our drones have an associated Raspberry Pi, so when powered but not armed, we download the log files from Ardupilot to the Pi over a serial port (implied relatively slow). Our log files can grow to 200MB or so, hence it is quite possible for an operator to power down while a download is in progress, hence leaving a partial file.
 I modified (hopefully not a hack) the logfile plugin to support a resume of downloading from where the partial download ended. From the initial tests the code appears robust, but this is only against a simulator and not field tests.
 If there is interest I would certainly share the approach and the code with the community where it could reviewed potentially improved. 

Cheers,

title: libmavsdk.so exports statically linked curl/openssl symbols causing conflicts with ROS2 FastDDS middleware
body:
Hi!. I've read that MavSDK is not really supposed to be used with ROS2 but nevertheless, I'd like to share a problem that I've found. 

When running a node with MavSDK under the hood (C++), I've been getting instant seg-faults until I switched from `rmw_fastrtps` to `rmw_zenoh_cpp`. I've tried to dig into the problem using AI since I don't really understand such a low-level subject.

It provides the following explanation:

1. Problem: MAVSDK exports its statically linked curl symbols into the global dynamic linker namespace. When used alongside ROS2 with rmw_fastrtps_cpp, FastDDS resolves its curl calls to MAVSDK's internal version, causing a segfault in XMLProfileManager::loadDefaultXMLFile() at address 0xA.
2. Proof command:
```bash
nm -D /lib/libmavsdk.so.3 | grep "^[0-9a-f]* T curl_"
```
This shows curl symbols exported as public (T = global text symbol). They should be local/hidden.
The output of the command attached.

I'm a big fan of both MavSDK and ROS2 so I would appreciate the fix so I will able to use them without any workarounds.

Thank you for your work gentlemen!

[output.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26314048/output.txt)

title: Expose io_context for external event loop integration
body:
## Problem

Currently MAVSDK always owns its `asio::io_context` and runs it on an internal `_io_thread`. There is no way for an application that already runs its own Asio event loop (e.g. a drone autopilot written with Asio, or a ROS2 node using its own executor) to share the io_context with MAVSDK.

## Proposed solution

Add a `Mavsdk` constructor overload that accepts an `asio::io_context&`:

\`\`\`cpp
Mavsdk(Configuration configuration, asio::io_context& external_io_context);
\`\`\`

When constructed this way:
- MAVSDK does not start `_io_thread`
- The caller is responsible for calling `io_context.run()` (or integrating it into their event loop via `poll()` / `run_one()` etc.)
- All other behaviour is identical

## Design considerations

- Exposing `asio::io_context` in `mavsdk.h` means Asio becomes part of the public API. We may need a forward-declared wrapper or an `any_io_executor` variant to keep the public header clean.
- An alternative: expose a `run_once()` / `poll()` method that lets callers drive the event loop without exposing the type directly — but this is less idiomatic for Asio users.
- Related: `set_callback_executor()` already lets users redirect _callbacks_ to their own thread. This issue is about integrating the _I/O loop_ itself.

## Context

This came up after #2810 which migrated all internal I/O to a single Asio io_context. That PR is a prerequisite for this feature.

title: Feature Request: Upload mission raw with progress
body:
Hey! 👋
I noticed that the Mission plugin already has `uploadMissionWithProgress`, which is super handy for tracking how far along a mission upload is. It would be really cool to have the same thing for the MissionRaw plugin as well.
Right now, when uploading a mission via MissionRaw, there’s no way to observe the progress, which makes it tricky to show any kind of feedback to the user.
Having something like `uploadMissionWithProgress` in MissionRaw would be awesome — especially for larger missions where the upload takes a bit longer.

Thought it’d be a great addition. Thanks for all the work on this project! 🙏

```bash
#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>
#include <mavsdk/mavsdk.h>

struct Px4MissionService : public rclcpp::Node {
	mavsdk::Mavsdk sdk;

	Px4MissionService() 
		: rclcpp::Node("px4_mission_service"),

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	rclcpp::init(argc, argv);
```

title: Augment goto_location action for planes
body:
Hi, I was wondering if we could add the possibility to set the loiter radius when calling the **goto_location** action.

It is using the **MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION (192)** (https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_REPOSITION) MAVLink command whose third parameter is "Loiter radius for planes. Positive values only, direction is controlled by Yaw value. A value of zero or NaN is ignored."

I don't know about PX4, but this allows me to fly a plane with ArduPilot. However I would understand that it can make the API a bit ugly.

title: MavlinkDirect does not receive some messages via serial
body:
I think I have found a bug in MavlinkDirect. The following MAVLink messages are (almost never) received when sent via a serial port, and subscribed to by MavlinkDirect:

```
HEARTBEAT 
SYS_STATUS
POWER_STATUS
MEMINFO
NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT
MISSION_CURRENT
GPS_RAW_INT
```
There may be others, but these are the missing messages I've found so far in my testing.

Tested with MAVSDK version 3.15, installed from `libmavsdk-dev_3.15.0_debian12_arm64.deb`

### Test Code

I have two different C++ scripts/files that I am using for this testing:

* [mavlink_message_listener.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691963/mavlink_message_listener.cpp) - uses `mavsdk.intercept_incoming_messages_async` to print out **every** MAVLink message on the device. This seems to work accurately as far as I can verify with QGroundControl/MissionPlanner. So I do trust this script, and it is actually heavily based on one of the mavsdk examples IIRC.

title: Add mavsdk API for STATUSTEXT
operator<< for MavlinkPassthrough::Result missing MAVSDK_PUBLIC
body:
Title pretty much says it. Hit a linker error trying to stream a MavlinkPassthrough::Result to std::cout. Looks like the operator<< overload in the passthrough header is missing the MAVSDK_PUBLIC specifier that the equivalent MavlinkDirect one has, so the symbol doesn’t get exported.

In mavlink_passthrough.hpp (line 94):
`friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& str, MavlinkPassthrough::Result const& result);`

In mavlink_direct.hpp (line 126):
`friend MAVSDK_PUBLIC std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& str, MavlinkDirect::Result const& result);`

Adding MAVSDK_PUBLIC to the passthrough declaration should fix it I would think.
Building latest main on Rocky 8 using g++ 8.5.0

title: Race condition bug
body:
### Issue:
Specific race condition between [send_capture_status](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/3e26666176bad4a1df51575808fc05ec494abea9/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/camera_server/camera_server_impl.cpp#L1370)  and [send_tracking_status_with_interval](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/3e26666176bad4a1df51575808fc05ec494abea9/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/camera_server/camera_server_impl.cpp#L2140).

`send_capture_status` locks `_mutex`, before calling `queue_message` and locking `_mavlink_packet_mutex`, `send_tracking_status_with_interval` calls `queue_message`, blocking `_mavlink_packet_mutex`.
`send_capture_status` gets stuck waiting for `_mavlink_packet_mutex` and `send_tracking_status_with_interval` gets stuck for `_mutex`

title: Add support for disabling native heartbeat sending and triggering HEARTBEAT over gRPC
body:
I would like to contribute a feature that lets MAVSDK users disable internally generated HEARTBEAT sending and instead trigger transmission through gRPC.

The gRPC API would be a fail-closed, one-shot request to send a single MAVSDK-configured HEARTBEAT, not a toggle or persistent enable state. If the client stops calling, disconnects, or fails, MAVSDK does not continue sending heartbeats through that path. The client is responsible for calling at the desired rate (e.g. ~1 Hz).

The gRPC call would not set HEARTBEAT fields; MAVSDK continues to own message content (sysid, compid, mav_type, etc.). The call only requests that MAVSDK send its configured heartbeat.

Some integrations need an external process to control when MAVSDK sends heartbeats, while MAVSDK still constructs the actual MAVLink HEARTBEAT message. This avoids duplicating heartbeat construction outside MAVSDK.

**Proposed Solution**
- Add a configuration option (e.g. automatic_heartbeats_enabled) to disable native heartbeat sending.
- Add a gRPC API to trigger one configured HEARTBEAT per request.
- Optionally expose via mavsdk_server CLI (e.g. --no-automatic-heartbeats).

Default behavior stays unchanged.

title: Android: camera definition fails to load, Camera.getCurrentSettings() returns UNAVAILABLE
body:
## Description
I'm using MAVSDK Java / Android with `mavsdk_server` on an Android controller. The vehicle has a MAVLink camera component that advertises a camera definition (`camera_definition-ILX-LR1_Sony-40847.xml`). The camera is discovered correctly, but the MAVSDK Camera plugin never seems to load the camera definition, and `Camera.getCurrentSettings(componentId)` returns `UNAVAILABLE`.

This prevents reading the current camera settings through the Camera plugin. Setting camera params through other paths can still affect the camera, but MAVSDK cannot read back the settings.

After camera discovery, I can see the failure logs:
```
D/Mavsdk  : Component Camera 1 (100) added.
E/Mavsdk  : Cannot open file "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
D/Mavsdk  : Cache hit for camera_definition-ILX-LR1_Sony-40847.xml
E/Mavsdk  : Failed to open "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
I/Mavsdk  : Using cached file "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
E/Mavsdk  : tinyxml2::LoadFile failed: Error=XML_ERROR_FILE_READ_ERROR ErrorID=5 (0x5) Line number=0
E/Mavsdk  : Failed to load camera definition: "/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4
...
io.mavsdk.camera.Camera$CameraException: UNAVAILABLE: Unavailable
	at io.mavsdk.camera.Camera$19.onNext(Camera.java:2006)
	at io.mavsdk.camera.Camera$19.onNext(Camera.java:1999)
	at io.grpc.stub.ClientCalls$StreamObserverToCallListenerAdapter.onMessage(ClientCalls.java:468)
	at io.grpc.internal.ClientCallImpl$ClientStreamListenerImpl$1MessagesAvailable.runInternal(ClientCallImpl.java:667)
	at io.grpc.internal.ClientCallImpl$ClientStreamListenerImpl$1MessagesAvailable.runInContext(ClientCallImpl.java:654)
	at io.grpc.internal.ContextRunnable.run(ContextRunnable.java:37)
	at io.grpc.internal.SerializingExecutor.run(SerializingExecutor.java:133)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1100)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:624)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1572)
```

## Potential Source
This looks like it may be related to the `ANDROID` branch of the `get_cache_directory()` [function here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/fs_utils.cpp#L70). That code reads `/proc/self/cmdline`. On Android this is NUL-separated, and in our app the first arg includes a trailing NUL:
```
/proc/self/cmdline first-arg="com.dronebase.af.app.px4?" (hasEmbeddedNul=true)
```

The resulting cache path appears to be truncated to `/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4`. This is the package root but not the MavSDK cache directory `/data/data/com.dronebase.af.app.px4/mavsdk_cache`.  Because the process name still contains the NUL separator from `/proc/self/cmdline`, native file operations appear to truncate the path before `/mavsdk_cache`. 

There is already a [comment](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/fs_utils.cpp#L75) indicating that the trailing `\0` should be stripped, but the current check appears to dereference `line.end()`. Since `end()` is one past the last character, this does not reliably test the trailing byte. The package name can retain the NUL separator and produce a path that is later truncated by native file operations.

title: mavsdk.pc forces bundled private dependencies on shared-library consumers
body:
### Problem

The generated `mavsdk.pc` declares implementation dependencies as pkg-config private requirements:

```pkgconfig
Requires.private: libcurl jsoncpp tinyxml2
```

(Current `main` uses `nlohmann_json` instead of `jsoncpp`, but retains the same structure.)

For the prebuilt shared-library packages, these dependencies are bundled into `libmavsdk.so`. They are not exposed through MAVSDK's installed public headers and are not dynamic dependencies of the installed shared object. Nevertheless, pkg-config attempts to resolve the private modules when compiler flags are requested.

On a clean Debian 13 ARM64 system with MAVSDK 3.17.2 installed:

```console
$ pkg-config --modversion mavsdk
3.17.2

$ pkg-config --libs mavsdk
-lmavsdk

$ pkg-config --cflags mavsdk
Package libcurl was not found in the pkg-config search path.
Package 'libcurl', required by 'mavsdk', not found
Package 'jsoncpp', required by 'mavsdk', not found
Package 'tinyxml2', required by 'mavsdk', not found
```

This prevents the conventional command from working:

```sh
c++ example.cpp $(pkg-config --cflags --libs mavsdk)
```

CMake consumers using `find_package(MAVSDK)` build and run successfully on the same system.

### Package inspection

I reproduced this while producing and testing a Debian 13 ARM64 build from the v3.17.2 tag, and also confirmed that the official v3.17.2 Debian 13 AMD64 package contains the same `Requires.private` line.

For the ARM64 shared object:

```console
$ readelf -d /usr/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.17.2 | grep NEEDED
Shared library: [libstdc++.so.6]
Shared library: [libm.so.6]
Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
Shared library: [libc.so.6]
```

The installed MAVSDK public headers do not include curl, jsoncpp, or tinyxml2 headers. The package supplies the shared library and no static `libmavsdk.a`.

### Expected behavior

Installing the shared-library development package should be sufficient for:

```sh
pkg-config --cflags --libs mavsdk
```

Private implementation dependencies already incorporated into `libmavsdk.so` should not require their development packages on the consumer system.

### Suggested fix

Remove `Requires.private` from `mavsdk.pc` for shared-library builds/packages, or generate it conditionally only for a static installation whose final consumer genuinely needs those external archives.

This is related to #2475, which covers the separate hard-coded CI-prefix problem in the generated pkg-config file.
